name: Great Beast Mutations
caption: Great Beast Mutations
rows: Roll twice on the table, ignoring this result if rolled again.

rows.name: Spawning Pit
entries: Your skin begins to crawl moments before vermin chew through your flesh and erupt from your body. {@dice 1d3} {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} {@creature Swarm of Crawling Claws|XMM|Swarms of Crawling Claws}, {@creature Swarm of Insects|XMM|Insects}, or {@creature Swarm of Rats|XMM|Rats} appear in unoccupied spaces within 10 feet of you. This also happens the first time you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB} after an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} check.

rows.name: Bloodless
entries: You cannot spend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} for any reason, including as the result of a spell or other {@variantrule Magical Effect|XPHB}.

rows.name: Corporeal Decay
entries: Your body begins to rapidly decay, giving you a corpselike appearance. When you gain this mutation, roll a number of {@dice 1d8;2d8;3d8;4d8;5d8;6d8;7d8;8d8;9d8;10d8;11d8;12d8;13d8;14d8;15d8;16d8;17d8;18d8;19d8;20d8;|d8s} equal to your character level and take Necrotic damage equal to the result. You have the Undead type in addition to other creature types.

rows.name: Lignify
entries: Your limbs stiffen and woody tree shoots pierce from beneath your skin. You have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (all movement types) is reduced by 5 feet per your level of {@condition Corruption|GrimHollowCG24}.

rows.name: Scion of the Beast
entries: You carry some of the Great Beast's corruptive nature. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action on your turn, you and another creature of your choice you can see within 60 feet of you each make a {@adventure Mutation check|GrimHollowCG24|20|Great Beast Mutations}.

rows.name: Third Eye
entries: You grow a third eye. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or remove the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Extra Digits
entries: Your grow several extra fingers. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to avoid being disarmed, but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Chameleon
entries: Your skin changes color in stressful situations. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks, but {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks.

rows.name: Oily Skin
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks made to escape a {@condition Grappled|XPHB|Grapple}, but you have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Cold and Fire damage.

rows.name: Corrosive Blood
entries: When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} for the first time after an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, creatures within 5 feet of you take Acid damage equal to your character level.

rows.name: Sticky feet
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} of 15 feet, but your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet.

rows.name: Luminescent
entries: You glow with {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} to a range of 30 feet. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Thinning Blood
entries: Your bodily fluids become thin and watery. You have the {@condition Bleeding|GrimHollowCG24} condition.

rows.name: Stone Shell
entries: Your skin swells and hardens into a tumorous rocky texture. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing and Slashing damage, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Acid and Thunder damage.

rows.name: Arcane Conduit
entries: Your body becomes a conduit of magic. Add your current {@condition Corruption|GrimHollowCG24} level to your spell save DC and your spell attack rolls. When you cast a spell using a spell slot, make a {@adventure Mutation check|GrimHollowCG24|20|Great Beast Mutations}.

rows.name: Malformed Wings
entries: Spiny, tattered wings burst painfully from your back, giving you a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet. You cannot move by any other means.

rows.name: Blood-Fueled Frenzy
entries: If you are Bloodied, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee attack rolls, and attack rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. On each of your turns, you must first move as far as possible toward the nearest {@status Bloodied|XPHB} creature you can see. If you are within 5 feet of it after moving, you must take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to attack that creature with a melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

rows.name: Eldritch Combustion
entries: Your body fills with unStable eldritch power. If you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you die instantly, and each creature within 20 feet of you must make a {@adventure Mutation check|GrimHollowCG24|20|Great Beast Mutations}.

rows.name: Permanent Transformation
entries: You gain the {@charoption Aberrant Horror|GrimHollowPG24|Aberrant Horror Transformation}. If you already have this or another Transformation, you move to the next stage of that Transformation instead.

name: Grievous Wounds
caption: Grievous Wounds

rows.name: Permanent Wound
entries: You sustain a grisly wound that may haunt you forever. Roll 1d10 on the {@table Permanent Wounds|GrimHollowCG24} table and apply the result.

rows.name: Festering Wound
entries: Your injury becomes infected, causing a fever. You have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws. A creature cannot ignore this instance of the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition through {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}.

rows.name: Internal Bleeding{@sup *}
entries: You suffer an internal hemorrhage and bruising. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by three times your character level.

rows.name: Wracked With Pain
entries: Your injury causes intense pain that limits your agility. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

rows.name: Concussion
entries: A brain contusion leaves you struggling to focus. You gain the {@condition Dazed|GrimHollowCG24} condition.

rows.name: Laceration
entries: lood wells unabaited from a deep injury. You gain the {@condition Bleeding|GrimHollowCG24} condition.

rows.name: Deep Wound{@sup *}
entries: You endure a blow that would kill many, but merely staggers you. When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you start with one failed {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}.

rows.name: Battered{@sup *}
entries: Your muscles ache and you have had the wind knocked out of you. You gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

rows.name: Injured Wrist{@sup *}
entries: You have badly sprained your wrist or fractured a bone in your arm and are unable to use it effectively. You are unable to hold objects in one of your hands and you cannot take actions that require that arm.

rows.name: Damaged Eardrum
entries: A blow to your head impairs your hearing. You have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.

rows.name: System Shock
entries: You suffer a severe nervous shock. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls.

rows.name: Injured Leg{@sup *}
entries: An injury to your leg or foot slows your movement. Reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 10 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} can't be increased, and you can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action.

rows.name: Torn Muscle{@sup *}
entries: This injury reduces your combat prowess. When you deal damage with a Weapon Attack or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, roll {@dice 1d4;1d6;1d8;1d10;1d12|1d4} and subtract the result from the damage dealt. Each additional time you receive this wound, increase the size of the die rolled (to 1d6, 1d8, 1d10, and 1d12). After reaching the maximum die size listed, replace further Torn Muscle results with Injured Leg.

rows.name: Stymied Recovery
entries: Your injury slows your overall recovery. The total number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} you can spend during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Alternative Rest System|GrimHollowCG24|Quick Rest} is equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

rows.name: Severe Swelling
entries: Your swollen injuries give you an uncouth appearance. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Close Call{@sup *}
entries: You narrowly miss an otherwise dangerous blow. Instead of being reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you have 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

footnotes: Results with a {@sup *} next to them can be taken more than once

name: Grymclover Forests; Becoming Lost
intro: Finding your way through a forest that's been mutated like this is exceptionally difficult due to the dense brambles, thick canopy, and low visibility. When a character makes a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to navigate to a specific location within the forest, consult the {@table Grymclover Forests; Grymclover Navigation DCs|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Grymclover Navigation DCs} table. On a failed check, they become lost and suffer a setback determined by the {@table Grymclover Forests; Becoming Lost|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Becoming Lost} table.
rows: Completely lost, the party gets turned around and ends the day at the edge of the forest where they initially entered.
Confused and wandering, the party ends the day up to {@dice 2d4} miles in a random direction away from their intended destination for that day.
Despite getting lost, the party recovers and ends the day only {@dice 1d4} miles away from their intended destination for that day.

name: Grymclover Forests; Corrupted Creatures
intro: Beasts, monstrosities, and even plants that venture into a grymclover forest will sometimes become suffused by the area's corrupting magic, twisting them with mystifying effects. At your discretion, you can use the following table to determine how a creature may have been warped by the corruption.
rows: The creature can use a bonus action to turn {@condition invisible}, as if by the {@spell invisibility} spell.
The creature can use an action to cast a 1st-level spell at will, such as {@spell bane}, {@spell entangle}, {@spell inflict wounds}, or {@spell magic missile}.
The creature regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point. If the creature takes radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn.

The creature is covered in dense brambles, which grant it a +2 bonus to AC and deals {@damage 1d6} piercing damage to any creature that {@action grapple|PHB|grapples} it or is {@condition grappled} by it at the start of each of its turns.

The creature has telepathy out to 120 feet and is aware of the presence of creatures within that range that have an Intelligence score of 4 or higher. It knows the distance and direction to each creature.

The creature has increased pain tolerance, gaining 30 temporary hit points whenever it finishes a short or long rest. If another creature hits it with a melee attack while it has these hit points, the attacker takes 5 necrotic damage.

name: Grymclover Forests; Corrupted Foraged Food and Drink
intro: The adverse effects that cause a grymclover forest to emerge provide additional danger by corrupting sources of clean water and food. A foraging character makes a DC 15 Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check. There's a {@chance 50|50 percent} chance that any food or water found in these forests has been corrupted. A DC 15 Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check or {@spell detect poison and disease} spell reveals if any foraged food or water has been corrupted. A creature that ingests corrupted food or water in this way must roll on the Corrupted Foraged Food and Drink table.
rows: The creature is {@condition poisoned} for {@dice 3d4} hours, even if they would normally be immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition.
The creature is {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour, even if they would normally be immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition.
The creature gains no beneficial effects from the food or water but suffers no other ill effects.

name: Grymclover Forests; Corruptive Influence
intro: The manipulative energy that corrupts a forest into a grymclover one can linger for centuries, if not longer. Such twisted magic can wrack the minds of travelers with doubts and fears. Characters within a forest must succeed on a DC 13 Intelligence saving throw whenever they finish a long rest or suffer from an effect from the Corruptive Influence table below. A character has disadvantage on saving throws against these effects if it is within 3 miles of a gateway to the plane of the Fey or the realm of shadows and dread. A corruptive influence lasts until the creature finishes a long rest or is targeted by the {@spell greater restoration|PHB} spell or similar magic.
rows: Your senses betray you, making it difficult to accurately judge or feel confident of your surroundings. For the duration, you have disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks.

Your feelings of aggression and mistrust are heightened. For the duration, you gain the following flaw, "I can only trust myself. If someone crosses me, I will defend myself by whatever means necessary."
You are overcome with sorrow and grief, threatening your hope and sense of self. For the duration, you have disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

You have the overwhelming feeling of being watched from the shadows at all times, preventing you from recovering from a short rest. For the duration, whenever you expend a Hit Die to regain hit points, roll the die twice and use the lower result.

name: Grymclover Forests; Example Dungeons Table
rows: A spiraling, spiked tower built by a legendary necromancer, such as Dendallen ({@link saddleb.ag/dendallen}), or an ancient {@creature lich}.
Roving bands of mindless undead loosely controlled by {@creature wight|MM|wights}, an inexperienced necromancer, or other powerful undead.
The grove and accompanying settlement of an old {@creature druid} circle that worshipped a wrathful, primeval god of nature.
Acolyte {@creature druid|MM|druids} follow the footsteps of their spiritual or literal ancestors, working to summon an avatar of their deity to the Material Plane.
A complex of huts and cottages belonging to a coven of {@creature green hag|MM|green hags} that dabbled in magic forbidden even by others of their kind.
One or more young {@creature green hag|MM|green hags} or {@creature dryad|MM|dryads} tapping into the corruptive enchantment for power and knowledge.
The lair of a powerful {@creature ancient green dragon} trained in druidic magic.
A mixture of {@creature kobold|MM|kobolds}, {@creature cultist|MM|cultists}, and {@creature cult fanatic|MM|cult fanatics} attempting to resurrect a long-dead dragon by any means necessary.
The ruined capital city of a nation of ambitious elves that delved too deeply into the arcane and druidic magic of ecological transmutation.
Various hostile plant life and even some sentient plant creatures nourished and empowered by the residual corruption of the forest.
A sprawling and decrepit estate manor, where a cruel {@creature vampire} reigned by blood and terror.
A group of {@creature vampire|MM|vampires} and their surviving spawn have fled from crusaders, plotting and preparing their vengeance.
A camp from which a terrifyingly large and vicious {@creature gnoll} band terrorized a vast swathe of the surrounding region.
{@creature Bandit|MM|Bandits} or other scavengers are using the dungeon as their base of operations, but the forest's magic is causing them to mutate.
Ruins containing a still partly active summoning circle, where an infamous diabolist released dozens of devils and demons into the world.
A jagged tear in reality itself is allowing various fiends to cross from the Lower Planes onto the Material Plane, potentially heralding a massive invasion on the horizon.

name: Grymclover Forests; Example Grymclover Jungle Random Encounter Table
rows: An arch of slowly-shifting brambles that acts as a gateway to the plane of the Fey ({@chance 50|50%}) or the plane of Shadow ({@chance 50|50%}) during a waxing crescent moon or new moon, respectively.
A {@creature grymhare|GriffonsSaddlebag2} (see Grymclover Stat Blocks) innocently lying in a stray sunbeam to lure in unwary prey.
A circle of {@dice 4d4} {@creature druid|MM|druids} that are developing a ritual to channel ({@chance 75|75%}) or cleanse ({@chance 25|25%}) the Grymclover Forest's corruption.

{@dice 1d10} {@creature gray ooze|MM|gray oozes} ({@chance 45|45%}), {@dice 1d6} {@creature ochre jelly|MM|ochre jellies} ({@chance 35|35%}), or {@dice 1d3} {@creature black pudding|MM|black puddings} ({@chance 20|20%}) milling about aimlessly.

{@dice 1d4} corrupted, predatory beasts ({@chance 60|60%}) native to the region, such as {@creature brown bear|MM|bears} or {@creature wolf|MM|wolves}, or corrupted dinosaurs ({@chance 40|40%}) like {@creature triceratops} or {@creature tyrannosaurus rex} (see {@table Grymclover Forests; Corrupted Creatures|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Corrupted Creatures} sidebar above).

The brambles of the forest encircle the party to impede travel. Each character must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} piercing damage and gain one level of {@condition exhaustion} from the constricting vegetation.

{@dice 1d10} {@creature bramble creeper|GriffonsSaddlebag2|bramble creepers} (see Grymclover Stat Blocks) ({@chance 50|50%}) or {@dice 2d8} {@creature archer flower|GriffonsSaddlebag2|archer flowers} (see Grymclover Stat Blocks) ({@chance 50|50%}) patiently waiting in ambush.

{@dice 3d4} {@creature awakened shrub|MM|awakened shrubs} ({@chance 40|40%}), {@dice 1d10} {@creature awakened tree|MM|awakened trees} ({@chance 30|30%}), or {@dice 1d4} {@creature shambling mound|MM|shambling mounds} ({@chance 30|30%}) originally made from the forest's natural plant life, but now corrupted by the forest's choking brambles.

{@dice 2d12} {@creature psybird|GriffonsSaddlebag2|psybirds} (see Grymclover Stat Blocks) ({@chance 50|50%}) or {@dice 1d4} {@creature cloverback toad|GriffonsSaddlebag2|cloverback toads} (see Grymclover Stat Blocks) ({@chance 50|50%}) stirring up mist and fog with their movements.

A {@creature grym-mage tyrannosaur|GriffonsSaddlebag2} (see Grymclover Stat Blocks) ({@chance 50|50%}) or {@dice 1d8} {@creature cyglops|GriffonsSaddlebag2} (see Grymclover Stat Blocks) ({@chance 50|50%}) hunting and scavenging, respectively.

The swirling mists thicken and grow acidic for the next {@dice 1d4} hours. At the end of each hour, a character must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 4d8} acid damage unless they are protected by shelters such as a tent, building, or another fog-proof barrier.

An unexpected dungeon or ruin (see {@table Grymclover Forests; Example Dungeons Table|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Example Dungeons Table}) that is younger than the forest's corruption ({@chance 80|80%}) or is the origin of it ({@chance 20|20%}).

name: Grymclover Forests; Grymclover Navigation DCs
intro: Finding your way through a forest that's been mutated like this is exceptionally difficult due to the dense brambles, thick canopy, and low visibility. When a character makes a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to navigate to a specific location within the forest, consult the {@table Grymclover Forests; Grymclover Navigation DCs|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Grymclover Navigation DCs} table. On a failed check, they become lost and suffer a setback determined by the {@table Grymclover Forests; Becoming Lost|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Becoming Lost} table.
rows: A location on the outskirts of the wood, or near a larger settlement
A location near the center of the forest or steeped in Corruption, like most dungeons and ruins are
A location that is lost or hidden, such as a portal to the Fey or Shadow planes, a secret settlement, or a magically cloaked dungeon or ruin

entries.name: Call of the Grave
entries: An angel of death is obsessed with your fleeting spirit, and wants you back. When you roll initiative at the start of combat, make a death {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw}. On a failed save, the GM chooses an undead creature with a CR equal to your level or lower. It appears at a point 120 feet away from you and joins the combat against you. The creature knows where you are at all times and pursues you unerringly. It vanishes when reduced to 0 hit points, when you die, or after 10 minutes.

entries.name: Memories from the Beyond
entries: The memory of death lingers. At the end of each {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}, describe how your character has tried to forget what dying felt like, then make a Wisdom {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} with a DC set by the GM based on your answer. On a failed save, you gain one level of {@condition exhaustion} that lasts until you are subject to {@spell greater restoration} or similar magic, or until you spend 30 days in focused downtime to make peace with your memories.

entries.name: Obscure Purpose
entries: A greater power allowed you to come back for a reason. This might be a god such as the {@deity The Matron of Ravens|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Matron of Ravens} that you can now commune with, or an obscure supernatural being. This consequence might be an opportunity to become a {@class cleric} or {@class paladin} of this god, or to take levels in the {@class warlock} class. Alternatively, if you choose not to swear a covenant with this entity, or if you disobey their requests, roll again on this table. You suffer the new consequences until you adhere to the purpose of this entity or find a way to rid yourself of their attention.

entries.name: Persistent Wounds
entries: Whenever you fail a death {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw}, your hit point maximum is reduced by {@dice 2d10} until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}. If your hit point maximum is reduced to 0 in this way, you die.

entries.name: Secret Face
entries: You are no longer you, but a chaotic evil shapechanger who has taken your place. You play this duplicate and use your original game statistics until the duplicate is killed or until this consequence is otherwise overcome. The GM determines where your soul is actually being held captive—possibly in the afterlife for which you were intended, or in your double's malign realm.

entries.name: Hunger for Death
entries: Once per day, you or the GM must decide that you use the following reaction: When you see a creature you perceive as hostile or potentially hostile and your distance to that creature is equal to or less than your speed, you immediately and aggressively move your speed toward that creature, then make one melee attack against it. You have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on the attack roll if your attack is unexpected.

entries.name: Opaque Thoughts
entries: You obsessively recall the sensation of life tearing you from the jaws of death. These ever-present memories fill your mind, making you immune to any effect that would sense your emotions or read your thoughts. Likewise, other creatures have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks made to ascertain your intentions.

entries.name: Unearthly Awareness
entries: Your ordeal left a mark upon your soul, which now shudders in the presence of the undead. You know whenever an undead creature is within 30 feet of you, and you don't have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} on attacks against {@condition invisible} undead within this range. This constant awareness is distracting, however, and you have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) and Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks while any undead creature is within 30 feet of you.

entries.name: Bond of Vengeance
entries: You have returned as a revenant, bearing an unquenchable spark of hatred for the creature that killed you. As an action, you can focus on this spark to immediately learn the distance and direction to any creature that has killed you. If that creature is on a different plane, you learn only that information. If a creature that killed you dies, you immediately know. If you are within 120 feet of a creature that killed you, you have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} on attack rolls against any other creature.

entries.name: Never Again
entries: You don't fall unconscious when reduced to 0 hit points. Instead, you remain conscious until you end your turn without having attacked a creature or cast a spell of 1st level or higher. While you have 0 hit points, you have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on attack rolls, your attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d10} damage on a hit, and attack rolls made against you have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage}. You make death {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1} as normal, including suffering a failure when you take damage. Additionally, whenever you take damage while at 0 hit points, your hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

Ancient hoard, Dwarven city's treasure trove, or Dragon-hoard

name: Hopeful Omens
rows: A bear with pure white fur stands upon a rise, staring up at the stars before wandering away.
The sun, warm and bright, pierces through the overcast skies to illuminate the area around you.
Two ravens wait until you notice them on a nearby perch before croaking and flying away.
A grey wolf appears for a moment, seems to nod to you, then withdraws into shadow.
The sparks rising from the fire twist into familiar runes before scattering into the night.
Nine hand-sized stones form a perfect circle ahead of you.
A single flower blooms amidst the snow, a splash of color against the white.
For a moment, you hear the clicking of the weaver's loom in the wind.
A stranger in a tattered cloak stands in the shadows watching you with a single gleaming eye
You find a small stone with a pattern not unlike a rune scratched upon it by an unknown hand.
A bright, fiery light burns itself across the sky, heading North.
Behold! The Bifrost shimmers in the night sky!

name: Hot Items
rows: Multiple parties. Roll twice on this table, rerolling 1s.
A powerful bandit lord has caught wind of the item and is looking to take it for selfish gain.
A valiant hero wishes to see the item returned to the place from whence it came.
The item was stolen from a wealthy noble's collection. The noble has hired experienced bounty hunters to retrieve it.
The item has been magically tied to a legendary entity of great malice that requires it to restore its faded power.

name: Isle of Loki Encounters
rows: {@dice 1d2} {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} hunt for walruses along the coast. If they spot the PCs, they attack. The giants know of Loki's Hall but have never been inside the glacier and are not allied with the cultists there.
{@dice 1d3} {@creature Lindwurm|ToB1-2023|Lindwurms} skate across the frozen plains looking for prey. They are keen to add some humanoid flesh to their diet.
{@dice 2d4} hungry {@creature Winter Wolf|XMM|Winter Wolves} stalk a wounded {@creature Mammoth|XMM} (hobbling on HP 65) across the tundra. The wolves happily attack any PCs who get in the way.

An earth tremor causes a nearby snowdrift to collapse on the party (use the crumbling monument hazard in {@i ToV Game Master's Guide} or {@hazard Rockslide|XDMG} hazard in {@i D&D Dungeon Master's Guide}). The snowdrift deals 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Bludgeoning damage and 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Cold damage.
A {@creature Young White Dragon|XMM} flies over the PCs' heads. It attacks but retreats quickly if they prove formidable targets.
A {@creature Rime Worm|ToB1-2023} erupts from the snow and attempts to drag a character back into its hole to devour.

name: Jerbeen Figurines Table
rows: {@item Breath of the Wind-Touched Jerbeen Figurine|HumblewoodTales|Breath of the Wind-Touched}

A cheaply made figurine, it is little more than broken pieces of wood assembled into a roughly humanoid shape. Said to be made from branches the Wind-Touched brushed up against as she flew through the forest.
{@item Gift of the Wind-Touched Jerbeen Figurine|HumblewoodTales|Gift of the Wind-Touched}
A figurine carved from a single piece of wood, it appears hastily made, but it does vaguely resemble a jerbeen. Said to be carved from wood from the Greenkeeper farmstead.
{@item Grace of the Wind-Touched Jerbeen Figurine|HumblewoodTales|Grace of the Wind-Touched}
An ornate figurine of a jerbeen with wings carved with an impressive level of craftsmanship. Said to be made of branches gifted by the Wind-Touched from her own home in the forest.

name: Journey Events Table
rows: The fatigue saving throw DC increases by +3. In addition, if the check fails, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw*. On a failed save, the target is reduced to 0 hit points. On a successful save, the target loses half of their maximum hit points (rounded down).

The fatigue saving throw DC increases by +2. In addition, if the check fails, everyone in the Company gains 2 ({@dice 1d3}) Shadow points (Charisma saving throw* to resist, see {@book Chapter 8|TLotRR|4|Saving Throws Against Shadow}).

The fatigue saving throw DC increases by +2. In addition, if the check fails, the target gains 1 Shadow point (Wisdom saving throw* to resist, see {@book Chapter 8|TLotRR|4|Saving Throws Against Shadow}).
The fatigue saving throw DC increases by +1. If the check fails, the DC increases by +2 instead, and the length of the journey increases by 1 day.
The fatigue saving throw DC increases by +1. If the check succeeds, reduce the length of the journey by 1 day, to a minimum of 1 day.
The fatigue saving throw DC increases by +1. If the check succeeds, the DC does not increase, and the Loremaster improvises an encounter that favours the Company.
If the check succeeds, everyone in the Company gains {@variantrule inspiration|PHB}.
footnotes: * The DC for this saving throw equals the DC of the ability check (see Resolve the Event, below). The saving throw has disadvantage if it is autumn or winter.

name: Journey Roles
rows: In charge of all decisions concerning route, rest, and supplies.
In charge of finding food in the wild.
In charge of setting up camp, opening new trails.

name: Land of Hot Water Common Ingredients
Land of Hot Water Uncommon Ingredients
Legendary Benefits and Dire Consequences
rows: For 1 minute, once on each of your turns, if you successfully hit a target with a weapon attack, you can make another attack against the same target.
A nearby foe gains an ally in the form of a creature with a CR equal to half of the target foe's CR.
For 1 minute, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks and saving throws to avoid or escape a grapple.
For 24 hours, whenever you succeed on an ability check, you take {@dice 1d4} Force damage.
Foes within 5 feet of you have Dis{@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their weapon attacks against you for 1 minute.
All weapon attacks against you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} for 1 minute.
For 8 hours, double your movement {@variantrule Speed|XPHB|Speeds}.
For 8 hours, halve all your movement {@variantrule Speed|XPHB|Speeds}.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws for 1 hour.
For 1 hour, each time you succeed on a saving throw, there is a 50 percent chance you actually fail. Once you fail from a save due to this, the consequence ends.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you cast {@spell Greater Invisibility|XPHB} on yourself without expending a spell slot.

For 1 minute, each spell you cast has a {@chance 30|||You Cast the spell|The Spell failed} chance of failing. A failed spell doesn't expend a spell slot, but it does expend the action used to cast it.
For 24 hours, you can use the {@action Help|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can {@action Help|XPHB} other creatures from up to 30 feet away.
For 1 hour, if two enemies are within 5 feet of each other, and both are within 30 feet of you, they have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks.

name: Local Happenings Table
rows: "We got hit by a real banger of a storm two weeks ago. Folks say they saw someone flying in the gale, but no one's owned up to doing something so daft. Who could it've been?"

"A few days after the storm hit, a ship flying no flag docked at the harbor. A group of vulpin in dark garb disembarked, and then the ship left! They've been hassling folk for information about a raptor that blew in on the storm. I don't know anyone like that. D'you?

"My friend {@creature Arlowene Lum|HumblewoodTales} hasn't been seen much since the storm. She's been holed up in 'er lighthouse for nigh on two weeks now! {@creature Velma Leicester|HumblewoodTales|Velma} over there is 'er apprentice, but she's been awfully quiet lately. Perhaps you could try talking to 'er?

"A talonful of raptors have gone missing for days at a time, like ol' {@creature Hedy Crest|HumblewoodTales} over there. Once they came back, they didn't even know they'd disappeared. Listen strangers, dangerous things are happening here. You should leave before you get yourself involved. Oh, now, don't worry. We're hardy sailin' folks around here, and we can handle ourselves!"

name: Lost Memories
caption: Lost Memories
outro: A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell reverses this effect and restores the victim's memory.
rows: The target becomes deeply suspicious of a character or NPC of the GM's choice. They gain the following flaw: "I know they are seeking to betray me. I have to act first—it's me or them!"
The target forgets all memories of a loved one of the GM's choice. The next time the target sees them, it's as if they are meeting them for the first time.
The target becomes stricken with doubt and gains the following flaw: "The world is out to get me, and I can't win. I may as well give up now."
The target forgets how to speak in one language known, decided by the GM.
The target forgets the location of something important to them, of the GM's choice. It may be the location of a goal, their home settlement, or a hidden treasure.
The target loses an inconsequential memory such as what they ate a few nights ago or the name of an unimportant NPC.

entries.name: Elderberry Everwine
entries: This fine everwine is made from elderberries specially cultivated by forest vintners. It is highly prized among the Alderheart elite for its heady bouquet and dry sweetness.

entries.name: Noble's Jewelry
entries: A set of designer jewelry is fit to adorn any high-society socialite. When worn with a set of fine clothes, it allows you to pass for a noble. The jewelry can be custom made, in which case it costs an additional 10 gp.

entries.name: Perfume
entries: This aromatic liquid is made from rare ingredients, including floral extracts, wakewyrm ambergris, and essential oils. When daubed lightly on the skin, fur, or feathers, it leaves you smelling pleasant for 8 hours. It comes in a small, stoppered crystal vial containing 20 uses.

name: Making Custom Antronec Guild NPCs; Bonds
rows: I've invested a lifetime of effort into my business, growing it from the ground up.
A fellow Guild crafter was my mentor, they taught me everything I know about the craft.
Now that I can't work as much, I've taken on a number of skilled apprentices. They will be my legacy.
The craft itself is everything to me. If I had no outlet for my artistic vision, I'd have nothing worth living for.
I pour a piece of my soul into each piece I make. My life's work and I are one and the same.
{@homebrew Reroll.|No 6th option was present in source on this table, adding reroll since there wasn't anything.}

name: Making Custom Antronec Guild NPCs; Flaws
rows: I'm certain that people are plotting against me, making it difficult to trust others.
I've done horrible things to attain my position, and am plagued by my guilt. Should anyone uncover my deeds, I'd be ruined.
I can never work hard enough, fast enough, good enough to compete with my rival in the guild, and the frustration makes my temper short.
In pursuit of wealth, I take reckless risks I probably shouldn't, but can't resist.
I'm so focused upon my future ambitions and goals, that I'm blind to those I trample on my path forward.
My cutthroat business dealings have whittled away what few emotions and cares I had in the world, making me overwhelmingly cynical.

name: Making Custom Antronec Guild NPCs; Ideals
rows: {@b Perfection.} I cannot permit even one imperfection to spoil my craft. (Lawful)
{@b Self-improvement.} If each project is better than the last, my life is worthwhile. (Good)
{@b Beauty.} A true crafter brings utility and artistic wonder into the world. (Good)
{@b Hard Work.} I may not be as talented as others, but I compensate by giving all of my effort. (Lawful)
{@b Ambition.} I care about success, and in Antronec, the gateway is climbing the Guild ranks. (Any)
{@b Change.} A significant portion of art is how it changes the world, for better or worse. I want my work to move civilizations and mountains. (Chaotic)

name: Making Custom Antronec Guild NPCs; Personality Traits
rows: I easily get distracted by the small details of life, losing track of the big picture.
I'm incredibly competitive with the crafters within my own guild.
I speak far too quickly, as I'm eager to finish conversations and return to work.
To cover my lack of artistic flair, I have to absolutely gush with charm and suave salesmanship.
I'm such a horrible liar that I never make as much profit as others do.
I'm a horribly brusque businessperson, but I stick with it because of my devotion to the art.

name: Making Custom Druid NPCs; Bonds
rows: I witnessed a horrible act from a corrupt member of the Circle, but have no proof.
I seek to recover my family's tome of lineage, lost two generations ago.
I have a long-standing rivalry with another member of the Circle.
A mentor of the Circle took me in as a youth, I owe them everything.
An innocent family member is imprisoned in the Penitentiary.
I've been charged by the Spire to seek out arcane knowledge.

name: Making Custom Druid NPCs; Flaws
rows: I am so accustomed to lying and keeping secrets that I struggle to tell the truth.
I struggle to prevent myself from immediately executing judgment when I witness a crime.
I'm so focused on gathering knowledge that I find it painful to share it with others.
My exacting standards of self-perfection drive me to the brink of exhaustion on a daily basis.
I would set the world ablaze if tasked to do so by the Circle.
I truly believe that the world would be better off under the control of dragons instead of mortals.

name: Making Custom Druid NPCs; Ideals
rows: Justice. It's a lifestyle I take seriously. (Lawful)
Wisdom. Our way of life requires the constant advice of our forebears. (Neutral)
Responsibility. As a member of this proud tradition, I must strive for excellence. (Lawful)
Knowledge. The Circle's success thrives on secrets and research. (Neutral)
Order. Society would crumble without the Circle's firm guiding hand. (Lawful)
Patience. The Circle must patiently reap, that we may eventually sow. (Any)

name: Making Custom Druid NPCs; Personality Traits
rows: I struggle to control the drive to hoard wealth while in dragon form.
I'm constantly driven to keep things around me clean and orderly.
I have a nasty habit of snacking on rodents while in dragon form.
I always have change jangling in my pockets.
I hate that there are secrets I'm not allowed to know.
I often find my facial expressions to be unintentionally stoic or intimidating.
Random trivia is the coinage for my intellectual hoard.
I'm always more confident and comfortable when transformed.

name: Making Custom Durheim NPCs; Bonds
rows: I joined the monastery seeking peace and now that I've found it, I'll defend it to the end.
I'm training hard so that one day, I will be able to find and release the lost soul of a family member.
I struggle to feel peace outside the monastery, it keeps me anchored.
I feel aimless whenever I return to the monastery—I feel most alive when I'm investigating a haunting.
The monastery guards the border between the Material and Ethereal Planes, preventing conflict wherever we can.
Everyone says I'm too fidgety to ever find inner peace through meditation, but I'm going to prove them wrong one day.

name: Making Custom Durheim NPCs; Flaws
rows: Growing up in the monastery, I've been sheltered from the outside world, so I'm a bit clueless about most social interactions.
I focus so much on the Ethereal Plane, I often lose track of or downright ignore events on the Material Plane.
My forays into deep meditation have left me feeling detached from my physical body, it sometimes feels like a burden.
I don't sleep often or well, due to nightmares about some of my more horrifying ghost hunts.
I've grown so accustomed to following my superiors' requests, that I sometimes struggle to think or act for myself.
I secretly long for the day I die, so that I can experience what it's like firsthand.

name: Making Custom Durheim NPCs; Ideals
rows: Order. Structure and manners are the key ingredients in the making of a good life. (Lawful)
Charity. Helping lost souls is a noble calling, and I fully embrace it. (Good)
Aspiration. I find joy in my work, and strive to be the best spiritual guide I possibly can. (Any)
Freedom. I struggle to follow the rules of the order, focusing instead on getting the job done. (Chaotic)
Honesty. I value truth above all, even if it hurts others' feelings. (Lawful)
Joy. I love to feel my spirits being lifted as I guide others to peace. (Good)

name: Making Custom Durheim NPCs; Personality Traits
rows: I'm infinitely optimistic about the potential redemption of every spirit, even those who cause great harm.
I enjoy the violent parts of hunting spirits too much but am striving to find peace with the aid of my fellow monks.
I've helped friends and family pass on, but am still deeply troubled and meditate often on the purpose of my own life.
I believe that every ethereal spirit that claims to be peaceful is nonetheless capable of causing harm, so I send them to their rest by whatever means necessary.
I'm terrified of ghosts, but I joined the order so that I can one day conquer my fear.
I was raised by the monastery, so I follow their rules and guidelines to the letter.

rows.name: Durable
entries: The hit points of this item are tripled.

rows.name: Unreactive
entries: This item resists corrosion and rot. If an environmental effect or creature would cause an item to become damaged (such as a gray ooze's Corrode Metal), roll a d20. On an 11 or higher, the item is unaffected.

rows.name: Lightweight
entries: This item weighs half as much as normal at no detriment to its strength or potential to do damage. If it is a weapon with the heavy property, it loses this property. If it doesn't have the heavy property, it gains the light property.

rows.name: Magnificent Finish
entries: This item's finish is on point and it is worth twice its normal value.

rows.name: Flashy
entries: This item looks really cool. While you wear or hold the item, you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|PHB}) checks against creatures that can see the item.

rows.name: Insulated
entries: If this item is clothing or armour, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws against environmental effects caused by cold weather. If it is a weapon or held item, you have advantage on saving throws against the heat metal spell while holding it. If it is neither armour, clothing, a held item, or a weapon, roll again.

rows.name: Grippy
entries: You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being disarmed of this item, or having it taken from you against your will. If the item is neither a held item nor a weapon, roll again.

rows.name: Quick Release
entries: If this item is armour or a shield, it is quick to equip or stow. The time to don or doff the item is ten times quicker (a shield takes either a bonus action or an action). If the item is neither armour nor a shield, roll again.

rows.name: Aerodynamic
entries: If the item has the thrown property or is ammunition, its normal and long ranges increase by 50% (rounded down; if the item is ammunition it increases the range of the weapon that fires it by 50% instead). If the item doesn't have the thrown property or isn't ammunition, roll again.

rows.name: Perfect Balance
entries: If this item is a weapon, whenever you roll a 1 on the d20 when you make an attack roll with it, you can reroll the d20 and must use the new result. If this item is armour or clothing, whenever you roll a 1 on the d20 when you make a Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|PHB}) check or Dexterity saving throw, you can reroll the d20 and must use the new result. If it is neither a weapon, clothing, or armour, roll again.

rows.name: Artisanal Craftsmanship
entries: If this item is a weapon, it has a +1 bonus to its damage rolls. If it is armour, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from nonmagical attacks is reduced by 1. If it is neither armour nor a weapon, roll again.

name: Manufacturing DC & Time
footnotes: {@sup *} This can include nonmagical instruments like a compass, telescope, or the mundane component of a magical wondrous item (as required in the Forging process). The component cost is entirely up to the GM's discretion; an instrument might cost the same as a longsword, while a bejewelled crown can cost far more!

rows.name: Poor/Shoddy/Abysmal Handiwork
entries: This item is not well made. If this item is a weapon, it has a -1 penalty to its attack and damage rolls. If it is armour, it has a -1 penalty to its base AC. If it is neither armour nor weapon, it gains the Fragile quirk, instead.

rows.name: Fragile
entries: This item is prone to breaking. If the item is a weapon, when you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll using the item, the weapon breaks. If the item isn't a weapon, whenever you suffer a critical hit, roll a d20 for each fragile item you wear, hold, or carry. On a 1, the item breaks and is no longer usable.

rows.name: Unwieldy
entries: This item is poorly balanced or interferes with your movement. Whenever you make an attack with this weapon, or make a Dexterity saving throw or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|PHB}) check while wearing or carrying it, and roll a 1 on the d20, there are consequences. If the item is a weapon, it flies 10 feet in a random direction. If the item isn't a weapon, you fall prone.

rows.name: Degradable
entries: Spending time in water or other reactive environments causes this item to degrade. Roll a d20 each time it emerges after being submerged in water, or each hour it spends in a corrosive environment. On a 1, the item breaks and is no longer usable.

rows.name: Noisy
entries: Something about this item squeaks or rustles. You have disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|PHB}) checks while wearing or carrying the item, even if the item is stowed away.

rows.name: Pungent
entries: This item has a distinctly off-putting odour. While wearing or carrying the item, you have disadvantage on Charisma checks against creatures that don't like bad smells, and creatures have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|PHB}) checks made to detect you by smell.

rows.name: Heavy
entries: This item weighs twice as much as normal.

rows.name: Garish
entries: The designs and colours in this item are all wrong. While you wear or hold the item, you have disadvantage on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|PHB}) checks against creatures that can see the item.

rows.name: Mediocre Finish
entries: This item looks like crap and is worth half its normal value.

rows.name: Under Insulated
entries: Something about this item conducts heat or is under-insulated. While wearing or carrying the item, whenever you take cold or fire damage, you take an additional 1d8 damage of the same type.

rows.name: Dangerous
entries: When you make an attack with this item, while wearing this clothing or armour, or while holding this held item, the range of values that result in a critical fail increases by 1 (e.g. from a result of 1, to a result of 1-2 on the d20).

name: Mutations
rows: Wave of Mutation. You gain any one mutation of your choice, then gain an additional randomly determined mutation. Then, all creatures within 60 feet of you gain 1 {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level. Instead of rolling to determine whether or not those creatures gain a mutation, each automatically gains 1 mutation.

Anomaly Locus. When you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can reroll the {@dice d20}. When you do, you trigger an {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Arcane Anomaly}. You must finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again.

Sanguine Appetite. You develop a taste for blood which intensifies when you're wounded. While you have the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} or {@condition Bleeding|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} conditions, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee attack rolls against other creatures with the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} or {@condition Bleeding|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} conditions.

Fledgling Wings. Bat-like wings painfully explode from your back. You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 40 feet during your turn. If you end your turn aloft, you fall. If you have 4 or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, your wings expand and your {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} increases to 60 feet, and you no longer fall when you end your turn aloft.

Wretched Bile. Bubbling contaminated ichor unconformably builds up in your guts, which you can vomit forth periodically. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage for each {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level you have gained. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. You can use your Wretched Bile a number of times equal to your {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

Terrible Stench. Your body emits a pungent odor which reeks of death and sulfur. Creatures who end their turn within 5 feet of you have gain the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of their next turn. Creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made to locate or track you.

Explosive Demise. You feel volatile growths inside your body radiating intense heat. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage. If you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} while you have the {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Contaminated} condition, you die and explode horribly in a shower of gore. Creatures within a 20-foot-radius must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw. Failure: {@dice 4d6} Fire plus {@damage 4d6} Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage.

Hallucinogenic Visions. Your perception of the world around you twists into a miraculous landscape of rainbows, flowers, and vibrant colors, like walking through a pleasant dream. All creatures appear beautiful, friendly, smiling, and whimsical to you.

Cryogenic Shift. Your body rapidly disperses heat as ice begins forming on your flesh. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage, but if you don't move at least half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} on your turn, you have the {@condition Frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition ({@dc 15}).

Nascent Delusions. You gain a randomly determined form of {@condition Drakkenheim Madness|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, which persists so long as you have the {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Contaminated} condition.

Electric Discharge. Strange glands filled with crackling energy appear on your body. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage. At the start of each of your turns, you deal Lightning damage to each creature within 5 feet of you. The damage equals a number of d6s equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. If you have 4 or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, the dice become d10s, and the range increases to 10 feet.

Hulking. If you are Medium or smaller, your size increases by one step (from Small to Medium, or Medium to Large). While your size is increased, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ability checks. You return to your normal size when you no longer have {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels.

Shrinking. If you are Small or Larger, your size decreases by one step (from Small to Tiny, from Large to Medium). While your size is decreased, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength ability checks. You return to your normal size when you no longer have {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels.

Vocal Warp. Your voice takes on a strange pitch and resonance determined by rolling {@dice 1d6}. 1: Alien Resonance; 2: Wet Gurgling; 3: Demonic Baritone; 4: Constantly Singing; 5: Distant Echoing; 6: Rasping Whisper.
Wasting. Body parts begin falling out of you. Roll {@dice 1d6} to determine which: 1–2: fingernails; 3–4: teeth; and 5–6: toenails.

Rotting Extremities. One of your body parts begins to blacken and wither. Roll {@dice 1d6} to determine which: 1–2: your lips; 3–4: your nose; 5–6: your ears. If you reach four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, they rot and fall off. You can still speak and hear, however.

Transforming Skin. Your skin begins to change. Roll {@dice 1d6} to determine the effect: 1: painful blisters which seep strange liquids; 2: cracking and peeling to reveal raw sinew; 3: strange patterns and runes; 4: welts and bruises which throb violently; 5: necrosis and rotting in patches; 6: lesions in otherworldly multi-colored hues.

Lambent Glow. You emit a dim octarine glow to a range of 10 feet. If you have four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, you instead emit {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} to a range of 30 feet.

Shedding. Each time you gain a {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level, some of your hair falls out in patches. Once you reach four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, all hair on your body completely falls out.

Ocular Tumors. An eyeball opens somewhere on your body for each {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level you have gained. If you have four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, you can see in all directions.

Alien Organs. You feel a bloated shift within your abdomen, as if something has been altered in your internal composition. Several of your organs have changed into something unrecognizable yet still functional. They're filled with alien black goo.
Shimmering Veins. Your blood veins glow through your skin, casting a faint octarine light.
Shadowless. You no longer cast a shadow, regardless of the light sources around you.
Flickering Presence. Your form flickers intermittently like a poorly tuned hologram.
Gossamer Hair. Your hair becomes fine and ethereal, floating gently as if underwater.
Sprouting Crystals. Small bits of delerium begin to erupt from your bones and through your skin. They itch painfully.

Burning Blood. FLAME ON! As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can give yourself the {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition. The Fire damage is a number of d6s equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down). While you have the {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition, you gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. You can end the {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition as an action. If the {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} damage reduces you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, your flesh burns away and only a skeleton remains.

Screaming Brain. You grow a sentient brain in your body, and it doesn't like you very much. It berates you and constantly questions your judgment, constantly wishing to escape the confines of your body.
Vestigial Limbs. Your body suddenly sprouts additional appendages. The limbs are not usable, however. Roll {@dice 1d6} to determine what grows: 1: fingers; 2: toes; 3: leg; 4: Arm; 5: tail; 6: head.

Transmuted Flesh. Your flesh and body transform into an seemingly inorganic material but you remain animate and alive. This doesn't affect your game statistics. Roll {@dice 1d6} to determine which material: 1: iron; 2: wood; 3: glass; 4: stone; 5: water; 6: plastic.

Otherworldly Resistance. The {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} growing in your body makes you strangely resistant to similar forces. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to a damage type. Roll a {@dice d10} to determine which damage type: 1–2: Necrotic; 3–4: Thunder; 5–6: Radiant; 7–8: Psychic; 9–10: Force. You can gain this mutation multiple times, rolling a different damage type each time.

Chitinous Plates. Shell-like growths appear all over your body, giving you a +1 bonus to AC. If you have four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, this bonus increases to +2.
Amorphous Form. Your bones and organs become gelatinous. You can move through a space as narrow as 6 inches wide without squeezing.

Spiked Growths. At the start of each of your turns, you deal 5 ({@dice 1d10}) Piercing damage for each {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level you have gained to any creature you are {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB}.

Aquatic Adaptation. You sprout fish-like fins and gills. You gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can breathe underwater. If you have four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, you can only breathe underwater. You can hold your breath outside water for up to 1 hour.

Cyclopean Vision. Your eyes merge into a single central eye, which you can use to cast the {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} cantrip. You use your choice of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

Spatial Displacement. You can cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} once for each {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level you have. You regain these uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Tentacled Limb. One of your arms becomes a fleshy tentacle. When you make a melee attack on your turn, increase your {@itemProperty R|XPHB|Reach} by 5 feet.

Spider Climb. You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

Whispering Voices. You gain telepathy to a range of 10 feet, but other people hear it as their own voice. If you have four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, the range extends to 60 feet.

Belly Maw. A toothy mouth appears on your stomach. You can use it to make a melee attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn against a creature within 5 of you. Its attack bonus is equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). If you hit with it, you deal Piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier, plus an additional {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage for each {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level you have gained.

Eyeless Sight. Your eyes become milky orbs. You gain {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} to a range of 10 feet. If you have four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, your eyes rot out, and dim octarine light burns in the sockets. Your {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} increases to 30 feet.

Arcane Blood. You gain an additional spell slot of the highest level you can cast (to a maximum of 5th level). If you don't have spell slots, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by an amount equal to your level. If you have four or more {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels, you gain two spell slots instead of one or increase your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} by twice your level.
Reversed Limbs. Your base walking {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet and your {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} distance is doubled.

Chameleon. Your skin turns translucent and changes color to match your surroundings. As an action, you can give yourself the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, which lasts until the end of your next turn or until you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell. You can use this ability only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 until the end of the current turn.
Magic Resistance. You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and magical effects.

Regenerative Flesh. At the start of each of your turns, if you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB} and have at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. The healed flesh regrows as knobby, scaled, alien hide.

Multiplied Senses. Your face sprouts additional eyeballs, ears, and noses. You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} checks as well as Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks.

Corrosive Mucus. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spit acid at a creature within 30 feet. Make a ranged attack against the creature. On a hit, you deal {@damage 2d10} Acid damage and the creature is {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} ({@dice 1d10} Acid).
Rampant Mutation! Roll twice, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls.

name: Mysterious Omens
rows: The shadow of one tree falls in a different direction than the trees around it.
The moon flickers like a torch for a moment before settling back into its usual place.
The air bears the scent of the sea, though the coast is far away.
A shadow passes overhead, yet no bird or beast is in the sky.
A single sharp animal tooth stands upright, stuck into the ground, but no beast is nearby.
The ground rumbles faintly, and in its grumbling can be heard sounds that seem like words.
An unseen bird sings a mournful song that echoes in the forest.
Your own pouch rests on the path ahead, otherwise untouched and undisturbed.
A faint rune appears on a nearby surface, but it is gone when you look closer.
A flock of birds bursts out of cover, momentarily forming a rune-like pattern before dispersing.
The nearby water ripples as if disturbed, but nothing appears to have caused it.

name: Permanent Wounds
caption: Permanent Wounds

rows.name: Fatal Wound
entries: Through an unrecoverable injury, you have been fatally wounded. You are now dead but can be brought back through normal methods.

rows.name: Lost Arm{@sup *}
entries: A serious injury disables or destroys one of your arms. You can't use that arm to wield a weapon or a shield, or to perform the Somatic component of a spell.

rows.name: Lost Leg{@sup *}
entries: A serious injury disables or destroys one of your legs. Reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 15 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} can't be increased, and you can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. If you receive this result again your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by another 15 feet (to a minimum of 5 feet).

rows.name: Lost Eye{@sup *}
entries: You lose an eye. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight. If you receive this result again, you gain the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition.

rows.name: Dizzy Spells
entries: Undertaking vigorous activities leaves you addled. On odd numbered combat rounds, if you take an action, you cannot take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} until the start of your next turn. If you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you cannot take an action until the start of your next turn.

rows.name: Scarred Lungs

If you are not {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, attack rolls made against you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

rows.name: Old Pain

name: Road Encounters Table
rows: The party comes across a lemonade stand run by a mother mapach and her daughter. One cup costs 2 cp.
On the road, there's a large patch of snow mysteriously covering the ground. Near it are two large sleds made of wood.
A well-loved doll that looks like a strig in armor is found on the road. There's a tag on it that reads, "{@creature Riffin, the Ash-Knight|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|Riffin} Plush."

There are two jerbeens fixing a wagon at the side of the road. A character can help the jerbeens fix the wagon by making a check. A successful {@dc 12} Strength check helps set the wagon back on its axle. The jerbeens reward the party with two loaves of freshly baked bread.

A small stream runs by the path. A gallus family is enjoying a toy boat race. Adults and children alike are running along with the small ships made of leaves. If someone in the party has control over water or similar magic, they can help one of them win the race.

A rainstorm hits, muddying the road and making it difficult to continue. The party can seek shelter for two hours until the rain stops, though doing so will cost them time and expose them to more of the road's dangers. If they do this, choose or roll an additional encounter for their journey. Should they instead decide to press on, each character must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a character takes one level of {@condition exhaustion}.

Two vulpins are arguing on the road, their wagons clearly damaged from running into each other. With a {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) or Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check, the vulpins can be persuaded to continue on their way. Otherwise, they start throwing fruit at each other and the party from their carts until the party leaves.

{@dice 1d4 + 2} {@creature Slimesworn Cultist|HumblewoodTales|slimesworn cultists} lie in wait around a clearing. They are posing as corpses and wait until a party member comes within range of one of them to launch their attack.

Three {@creature Cursed Slime|HumblewoodTales|cursed slimes} and a {@creature black pudding} surround a traveling jerbeen and her son and will attack them unless the party draws their attention. The mother and child use the {@creature jerbeen commoner|HumblewoodTales} stat block. If saved, they thank their protectors with a bushel of apples.

The road winds between dense trees in this dark patch of forest and is blocked by a nearly {@condition invisible} {@creature gelatinous cube} that strayed here from the swamp. A group of bandits composed of two {@creature Jerbeen Thief|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|jerbeen thieves}, a {@creature strig berserker|HumblewoodTales}, and their leader, a {@creature mapach brute|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}, have taken advantage of this situation and are waiting to spring a trap once anyone becomes stuck in the ooze. The bandits are well hidden in the undergrowth and can be spotted with a successful {@dc 17} {@skill Perception} check, while the cube can be spotted and avoided with a successful {@dc 15} {@skill Perception} check.

name: Ruins Along the Greenway
intro: The Greenway is lined with many ancient ruins. If the Player-heroes decide to investigate such a site during their travels between Fornost Erain and Tharbad, the Loremaster can roll a {@dice d12} and use the following table.
rows: Long ago, wars raged across these lands as kingdoms fought against the armies of the Witch-king and each other. This tomb once held a great captain, but now it is only home to {@creature Fell Wraith|TLotRR|Fell Wraiths} from ancient Angmar who will harass and delay the company.

Stumbling upon the ruins of an abandoned roadside stable, the Player-heroes see a wild steed grazing in the grass. The majestic beast can be calmed with a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, then the horse can be ridden.

A battered tower stands a little distance from the road. A crescent moon is carved in stone upon its arched entryway. If the Player-heroes climb to its top on a night with a crescent moon, they find a single soldier standing watch. The guard politely asks if they are there to relieve him and if they say yes, the soldier bows and then heads downstairs–if any follow, they lose sight of the guard.
A small ring of white stones, overgrown with beautiful wildflowers lies not far off the road. No dangerous natural predators will cross the circle.

One afternoon, the Player-heroes meet an Elf who asks to walk with them for a time. She tells them that she is composing songs to honour Menelmacar who will arrive soon. If the heroes have patience with the minstrel, then they are in for a night of song and celebration. Each hero gains inspiration. If they are rude or impatient with the Elf, she excuses herself before nightfall and they gain no benefits.

A {@creature Southerner Raider|TLotRR} is hobbling up the Greenway, masquerading as an injured farmer. He asks the characters to walk with him to his nearby homestead, but when they arrive they find it to be a ramshackle barn where several of the Raider's allies ambush the Player-heroes.

A long stone wall follows the Greenway for a time here, and a handful of Orcs crouch beneath the wall, waiting for the Player-heroes to pass so they can ambush them. A {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check detects their presence.

A great mound of stones has been scattered near the road, a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals a large barrow has been dug down into the wet earth. Unfortunately, this makeshift tomb has become the lair of a {@creature Barrow-wight|TLotRR}, who will attack anyone who intrudes upon its resting place.

Once the farmhouse of someone who lived upon the Greenway, it is now a ruined pile of burnt rubble. A {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals that the occupants did not escape the fire, and that several appear to have been slain by Orc arrows before the flames took them.

A wandering Southerner, weary and travel-worn, asks for the Player-heroes' charity by letting him share their food and fire for the evening. If treated kindly, he will provide them with many stories about his distant country.

The characters come upon the corpse of a Man slain no more than a few days ago with vicious cuts and Orc arrows. His clothing is tattered, and a small brooch is clasped under his cloak, in the shape of a rayed star. Anyone who succeeds on a {@dc 10} Intelligence check can identify him as a {@race Ranger of the North|TLotRR}. If his brooch is returned to his people, a small favour might be asked in return.

The Player-heroes come upon a small keep some distance off the Greenway, tended by a lordly old man who offers them hospitality. If they accept and treat him well by making a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}), check that night they will dream of the glory of the towers of Annúminas and the shining shores of Lake Evendim. By dawn, they reduce their Shadow by 1, though in the morning the kindly old lord is gone, and there is no sign of the keep having ever been inhabited.

name: Ruins and Broken Stones
intro: Characters exploring the North Downs will often stumble upon ruins and ancient testimonies of the war that destroyed this place. The Loremaster can roll on the following table to determine what they find.
rows: A group of {@creature Fell Wraith|TLotRR|Fell Wraiths} rise out of the darkness of a burned ruin that projects from the fields of the North Downs like a jagged wound. They attack, filled with malice for all who live and would dare to trespass on their long absent Witch-king's field of victory.

The Player-heroes uncover an inscription in {@language Adûnaic|TLotRR} (on a wall, a slab of marble, or on a mosaic floor, for example). A {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Old Lore|TLotRR}) check is required to translate it. The content hints at the whereabouts of one place among The Dome of Sight, The Throne Room of Arvedui, or The Records of the Last King (see {@book Fornost Erain|TLotRR|8|Fornost Erain}).
With a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, the Player-heroes discover that they are being shadowed by someone. The mysterious spy disappears after a few hours, or if called out.

The Player-heroes discover the remains of a stone house that is still accessible. Inscriptions allow them to identify it as the ancient home of a noble from Arthedain, but idle scrawls and foul symbols also indicate that the building suffered from the ruin that Angmar brought upon the city.

The Player-heroes stumble upon a group of {@creature Highway Robber|TLotRR|Highway Robbers} in the middle of plundering what might be a tomb. Whether or not they become violent depends on how they are treated by the Player-heroes. What treasures they have on them (if any) should be determined by the Loremaster, but their finds would typically be worth {@dice 1d3} g.

While travelling across the North Downs, the Player-heroes hear the galloping of steeds at full charge, the sound of steel on steel, and the cries of both the victorious and the dying. The sound appears and fades without warning, seeming to come from all around the characters.
The earth beneath their feet gives way, and the Player-heroes tumble into a chamber of a long-collapsed building.

The Player-heroes discover a helm that, though dented and weather-worn, looks like it could easily be repaired and polished. It bears the crest of the Kings of Arnor, and might once again protect a noble brow.

The Player-heroes share a dream where a warrior of Arthedain asks them to give their remains a proper burial. A {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check around their night camp uncovers a collapsed watchtower and the skeleton of a fallen guard.

The Player-heroes uncover a spiralling mosaic on the floor of a ruined building. A {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals a removable slab of marble. Under it lies a greater Hoard of treasure, hidden there before the city was plundered. Golden dishes, cups studded with precious stones, lacquered drinking horns, and a small armoury of items of worth is secreted here.
