name: Tier 1: Coast
rows: While making their way on or alongside a river, the PCs see a knocked over wagon up ahead. Two bodies lie among scattered crates. A horse screams as it attempts to escape the grip of a {@creature Saber-toothed Tiger|XMM}.
A {@creature Mahoru|ToB1-2023} slinks through the water of the fjord toward an unsuspecting fishing boat.
A {@creature White Dragon Wyrmling|XMM} soars above the half-frozen water, looking for tasty fish.
Two {@creature Beli|ToB1-2023} perch on an ice-covered stack of stone jutting up from the water, waiting for boats to pass by to cause mischief
A {@creature Giant Eagle|XMM} drops a severed human arm near the PCs, a cleverly sealed scroll-tube still tied to the limb's hand.
Six {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9|NPCs}) pull a small boat onto the shore, arguing over stolen wine casks and a shining golden torc.

A beautiful {@creature Selkie|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) lingers on the shore, idly twisting a strand of pearls in her hands as she beckons the PCs to come closer.
The body of a bedraggled {@creature Knight|XMM} from a southern land lies on the sand and rocks with four black arrows in her back.
A mist rises from the water, carrying the scent of honey and woodsmoke. Indistinct forms in the mist reach out for anyone caught within.
Four {@creature Pirate|XMM|Pirates} clamber over the wreckage of a recent shipwreck, convinced several precious golden armbands are hidden within. They react poorly to interruptions.

name: Tier 1: Forest
rows: Three {@creature Ravenfolk Scout|ToB1-2023|Ravenfolk Scouts} accuse the PCs of harboring or aiding an elven thief. If attacked, they are joined by two {@creature Swarm of Ravens|XMM|Swarms of Ravens}.
A {@creature Ratatosk|ToB1-2023} follows the party for a time to gather gossip. She asks a seemingly endless stream of questions, makes pithy observations, and generally is a good-natured pest.
A vengeful {@creature Druid|XMM} marches along three {@creature Twig Blight|XMM|Twig Blights} toward a village, bent on misguided revenge.
A {@creature Brown Bear|XMM} lurches out of the woods and attacks the characters. It is infected by a {@creature Fleshcrawler|NorthlandsWorldbook}.
In a clearing, a {@creature Skeljaskra|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) rests in the center of four standing stones. Around the creature's neck is a silver collar.

A haunting chanting echoes through the trees from a {@creature Witch Apprentice|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) conducting a ritual with two {@creature Twig Blight|XMM|Twig Blights} around a bloody altar. An unconscious form is slumped nearby, prepared for sacrifice.
Four {@creature Tough|XMM|Toughsjhj} sit around a campfire, drinking heavily and hurling insults at travelers. Anyone who fails to jest back is mocked as a coward.
A {@creature Dire Wolf|XMM} stalks the party from the trees, drawn not by hunger but by something the characters carry—perhaps unknowingly.
A tree encased in unmelting ice serves as a prison for an {@creature Ostinato|ToB1-2023}. Breaking the ice allows a contagious tune to enter one of the PCs.

While camping for the night, four {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} approach, led by a ghostly human warrior ({@creature Specter|XMM}). To finally rest, the {@creature Specter|XMM} needs its ancestral weapon (stolen by the son of the local jarl) and begs the PCs for aid.

name: Tier 1: Glacier/Tundra
rows: Six {@creature Axe Beak|XMM|Axe Beaks} spot the PCs across the windswept tundra. They utter hungry calls as they charge toward their next meal.
A lone {@creature Wolf Reaver Dwarf|ToB1-2023}, cloaked in blood and shame, travels homeward, the only survivor of a ruinous raid on a nearby town.
Five {@creature Tundra Gnoll|source|Tundra Gnolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) trail the PCs, remaining in sight but beyond bow range, waiting for the right moment to strike.
Four {@creature Blood Hawk|XMM|Blood Hawks} circle overhead. Their presence draws other foes, and the hawks dive to attack when the characters are distracted by another Encounter.
A wounded {@creature Giant Elk|XMM} staggers through tall snowdrifts while a {@creature Polar Bear|XMM} follows its bloody trail.

A green shrub laden with bright blue berries grows out of cleft in a stone rising from the glacier. Should any of these luminous berries be consumed, they provide the same effects as a {@spell Goodberry|XPHB} spell.
Thawed by the party's campfire, six {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} claw their way out of the frost to attack. How many more lurk beneath the frozen ground?
Five {@creature Pirate|XMM|Pirates}, frostbitten and delusional, stagger across the ice. They babble about a gold-laden ship now entombed beneath the glacier and guarded by a fell beast.
Three {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres} stomp across the tundra, arguing loudly about the kidnapped {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} they drag behind them. None have noticed the PCs yet.
Two {@creature Raven|XMM|Ravens} perch silently on a stone near the PCs, watching with dark eyes. If approached or attacked, they fly away, only to return hours later.

name: Tier 1: Hill/Mountain
rows: Five {@creature Giant Eagle|XMM|Giant Eagles}, charged to defend ancient ruins, mistake the characters for tomb-pillagers. They circle, screeching menacingly.
A {@creature Giant Goat|XMM} bursts from the underbrush, chased by four howling {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}. A torn leather lead dangles from the goat's neck.
Five dwarf {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} argue near the entrance to a narrow valley, unsure if they want to venture into the territory of a reclusive seer.

A particularly dim {@creature Great Ogre|source} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) blocks a narrow bridge. He demands one PC compete with him in a flyting contest or he will throw them into the gorge below.
Two rime-cloaked {@creature Ashwalker|ToB1-2023|Ashwalkers} crawl from a nearby ravine speaking in cracked voices of dragons before attacking.

The sound of metal on stone echoes from a wide cave. Inside, a {@creature Thursir Giant|source} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) directs four {@creature Kobold Warrior|XMM|Kobold Warriors} to carefully dig out a vein of bright metallic ore.
A mated pair of {@creature Griffon|XMM|Griffons} dives out of the snow-laden sky, claws grasping for the PCs' mounts.
An angry and colorfully cursing {@creature Vættir|ToB1-2023} stalks the hills, seeking the ones who plundered its burial mound. Its only lead is a scrap of cloth marked with a white fox symbol.

Six annoying {@creature Ice Mephit|XMM|Ice Mephits} laugh and taunt the PCs as they traverse an icy slope. They giggle madly, using their {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB|Fog Clouds} to conceal hazardous terrain.
A howl of magical cold wind blows through the area. All magical and non-magical light sources are extinguished.

name: Tier 1: Ocean
rows: As the party crosses a frozen fjord or river, six {@creature Rime Worm Grub|ToB1-2023|Rime Worm Grubs} burst from beneath the ice, drawn by the heat of living flesh.
A {@creature Mahoru|ToB1-2023} follows the ship. It doesn't attack as long as it is fed from time to time. After several hours it swims away.
The aurora flows in the twilight sky as a ghostly song echoes over the waves. The oars fall silent and tears glisten on the sailor's hardened faces. Then the song ends.
A longship drifts aimlessly, its sails torn and useless. Among the bodies scattered on the deck are six {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls} hiding in plain sight.
A rowboat bobs in the waves. Its only occupant is an exhausted {@creature Priest|XMM} of Njord who claims to have rowed to meet the PCs to deliver a divine message.
As night falls, icy winds roar from the North, driving sheets of sleet and razor-edged hail.
Several icebergs loom ahead, carved into crude giant faces and rune-marked with ancient warnings.
A ship crewed by twenty {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists} led by a {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM} approaches under a flag of peaceful trade, desperate to trade loot for healing supplies.
An abandoned ship rides low in the water, slowly sinking. The bejeweled chest still tied to the mast is actually a {@creature Mimic|XMM}.
A heavily laden longship foundered on the rocks is occupied by a dozen {@creature Giant Crab|XMM|Giant Crabs} that defend their new territory with deadly force.

name: Tier 1: Road
rows: A sick {@creature Commoner|XMM} collapses on the road ahead. The village well has been poisoned by a {@creature Brunnmigi|source} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) that attacks anyone who attempts to leave.
When he spots the PCs, a {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM} darts off the road, believing they are hunting him for breaking his oath to a cruel jarl.
Four {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} rudely question the characters about a lost noble. Their leader challenges a PC to a holmganga if she suspects they are concealing information about her charge.
The ghostly forms of slain travelers silently plead for aid from beneath the yew tree where they were murdered by bandits years ago.

Three {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} burst out of a wheat field screaming in panic. They are pursued by two {@creature Malrgotr|source} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) that have dark veins spreading across their bodies from a magical infection contracted in the nearby woods.

Ten {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} ambush two {@creature Huskarl|source|Huskarls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) hauling valuable wergild for their jarl. The {@creature Huskarl|source|Huskarls} bellow for aid as the foes close in.
A wounded {@creature Berserker|XMM} stands among the bodies of slain {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits}. Bloody and wary, she mistakes the PCs for more raiders.

Banging their swords on their shields, a group of {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} and a {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM} demand a toll be paid for traveling on the road. Secretly, they work for a neighboring jarl.
Five travelers (secretly Ragnarok {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultist}) offer mead and a warm fire. In the dead of night, they whisper grim prayers and attack.

The PCs come across a large puddle in the middle of the road that appears to have recently been formed. Examining it more closely, they realize it's a {@creature Hill Giant|XMM} footprint, and it leads toward a nearby settlement.

name: Tier 1: Town
rows: Three {@creature Priest|XMM|Priests} walk through town, demanding all listeners give offerings to Wotan. Refusing draws public scorn and possibly impacts their reputation.

The characters overhear a {@creature Spy|XMM} conspiring with an underpaid {@creature Huskarl|source} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) in a mead hall's dark corner, plotting to act against the jarl or his family.

As the characters approach a small village, shouts of alarm draw their attention to a group of frightened {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} preparing bows to defend against a circling {@creature Nidhogg-Blooded Drake|source|Nidhogg-Spawn Drake} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}), which is eyeing the settlement's sheep as its next meal.
Three surly, hungover {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} search for a fourth, left behind at one of the taverns they visited the night before.
Two {@creature Huskarl|source|Huskarls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) and four {@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM} hunt a dishonored outlaw. One PC bears a resemblance to the outlaw.
Four Ragnarok {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultist} led by a {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM} grab an innocent {@creature Commoner|XMM} off the street, intending them for a later sacrifice.
A {@creature Doppelganger|XMM} silently inspects a drunken {@creature Guard|XMM} lying unconscious outside a tavern.

A {@creature Guard Captain|XMM} angrily searches for a team of {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} that should have reported for patrol an hour earlier. Rumors swirl of trollkin raiders or, worse, cowardice.

An obnoxious visiting {@creature Jarl|source} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) travels through the market accompanied by four {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}. Their poor behavior is close to breaking the laws of hospitality.

A {@creature Vættir|ToB1-2023}, clothed in tattered clothing and armor, strides over to the bar to talk to the barkeep. Other patrons don't seem shocked at this. The undead warrior says something about needing help.

name: Tier 2: Coast
rows: Water surges onto the shore nearly enveloping a group of fisherfolk. The liquid becomes a {@creature Water Elemental|XMM}, which lashes out with water tendrils as it assaults the commoners for disturbing its rest.
A {@creature Lake Troll|ToB1-2023} leaps from the water to grab a pack animal or careless PC, before dragging its prey back into the water.
A band of {@creature Wolf Reaver Dwarf|ToB1-2023|Wolf Reaver Dwarves} loads a beached longship for a raid. One spots the PCs and shouts, "Come fight or drink—either earns a tale."

Just as the PCs see a {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM} and six {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) digging frantically in the sand near the shore, one hoists a locked chest out of the ground.

Screams echo across the fjord as a {@creature Hafgufa Spawn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) drags a half-smashed fishing boat beneath the waves. Several fisherfolk swim frantically for the shore.
The PCs come upon a shipwrecked {@creature Mage|XMM} sitting upon a driftwood throne, surrounded by wooden posts with faces drawn on them. He demands the PCs kneel before the king.

Two {@creature Fjord Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Fjord Trolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) hunt lazily by the shore, arguing in a deep growl whether dwarf-flesh tastes better sun-dried or brined. Nearby, a pair of {@creature Gilitrutt Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Gilitrutt Trolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) naps in the sun.

An old longship, half-buried in the sand, groans with every wave. Four {@creature Vaettir Drowned Raider|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vaettir Drowned Raiders} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) prowl the wreck in their rusted mail, eyes glowing with memory and malice.
A sinister {@creature Dwarven Ringmage|ToB1-2023} lairs in a dark seashore cave, guarded by four {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers}.
A Sea Giant wades through the ruins of a half-sunken temple, humming an ancient tune as he repairs the old masonry.

name: Tier 2: Forest
rows: Two {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thursir Giants} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) rip apart an isolated home as they drink from broken barrels of ale. A young {@creature Commoner|XMM} hides beneath the porch of the ruined farmhouse.

A dangerous looking Dwarven {@creature Northern Hunter|NorthlandsWorldbook}, flanked by two {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}, calls upon the PCs to halt and accuses them of trespassing on his jarl's private hunting ground.

A handsome traveler begs for help finding his lost lover in a nearby barrow. Later that day, he reveals himself as a bloodthirsty {@creature Skogsra|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}).
The body of a trollkin hangs from a tree, bound by ropes of braided skin. Two {@creature Redcap|ToB1-2023|Redcaps} take turns dipping their crimson hats in the blood pooling beneath the body.

The characters stumble into an ice-covered clearing where the ritual sacrifice of a {@creature Huskarl|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) is being performed by two of {@creature Boreas's Chosen|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}).
Something has ravaged the forest, knocking over trees and partially devouring a deer. A {@creature Savager|ToB1-2023} hunts nearby, already on the trail of the PCs.

A herd of six {@creature Giant Elk|XMM} stampedes through the party. The real threat is the pair of {@creature Berserker Trollkin|NorthlandsWorldbook|Trollkin Berserkers} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) chasing them.

The trail through the trees grows dark, and crude stick figures, bound with twine, fur, and feathers hang ominously from the trees. A shadowy child darts through the trees, leading travelers toward a {@creature Night Hag|XMM}'s lair.
A loud clamor is revealed to be a warband of six {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} chasing a {@creature Giant Boar|XMM} through the woods. They assume the characters want to steal their prey.
A Jotunheim raiding party consisting of a {@creature Hill Giant|XMM} and two {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres} crashes through the forest, not caring if they are heard.

name: Tier 2: Glacier/Tundra
rows: A starving {@creature Rime Worm|ToB1-2023} erupts from beneath the snow with a scream of shattering ice, jaws wide. Steam rises from its hide, and the snow collapses inward as it strikes.
Three {@creature Frostveil|ToB1-2023|Frostveils} drift silently across the snow, seeking out warm bodies to consume.
A jagged crevasse splits open beneath a PC's feet, revealing a frozen warrior entombed in the ice. His eyes open, and a whisper escapes his lips, "The gods are watching."
An {@creature Ice Maiden|ToB1-2023} steps from the storm, barefoot and beautiful. She smiles, offers her hand, and frost crawls across the ground toward anyone foolish enough to take it.
A {@creature Lindwurm|ToB1-2023} emerges from a splintered ice crack, lunging at the nearest PC.
A cloaked {@creature Runewright|NorthlandsWorldbook} stands motionless upon the snow-covered tundra, gazing at a dark stone monolith.
Howling wind becomes actual howls as a {@creature Swarm of Wolf Spirits|ToB1-2023} charges into view, hungry for blood.
The ground seems to tremble as a {@creature Frost Giant|XMM} charges out of the storm, bellowing his war cry.
The door of a snow-covered barrow groans open as the PCs near, revealing a {@creature Mallqui|ToB1-2023}, who offers wise council if approached peacefully.
A lone {@creature Mammoth|XMM} trumpets in panic as a {@creature Son of Fenris|ToB1-2023} bursts from the snow to leap upon its back, savaging the larger creature with hungry claws.

name: Tier 2: Hill/Mountain
rows: The soaring peaks seem to tremble as a blinding flash of lightning reveals the imposing figure of a {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}). She pulls more lightning out of the sky and charges toward you.
A lazy {@creature Hill Giant|XMM} reclines atop a stone-warmed rock outcropping, demanding exactly 10 CP for each traveler. She won't take any other coinage.

Five {@creature Wolf Reaver Dwarf|ToB1-2023|Wolf Reaver Dwarves}, muddy and bloody from an unsuccessful raid, block the path with shields in hand. They seek a worthy challenge and have chosen the PCs.
Four {@creature Ettin|XMM|Ettins} sit around a campfire arguing loudly about which head gets to eat first. Their bickering pauses when the PCs approach, then resumes about who gets to eat the PCs.

A significant argument between multiple voices echoes up ahead. A {@creature Thrudgelmir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) sits before a makeshift talf board, arguing with itself over how to play.
As penance for betraying its jarl, a {@creature Spectral Guardian|ToB1-2023} haunts the pass. It is drawn to those who have broken oaths.
A red-furred {@creature Nightgarm|ToB1-2023} feasts on the corpse of a {@creature Wolf Reaver Dwarf|ToB1-2023}, so far ignoring the approaching PCs.

Two {@creature Stone Giant|XMM|Stone Giants} laugh as they compete to see who can lob a boulder closest to the PCs. One tells the PCs if they move away before a winner is determined, they will attack.

Following the sounds of bestial screams, the PCs come upon an odd sight. A {@creature Grendelkyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) cowers behind a boulder as two other {@creature Grendelkyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} roar and pelt him with stones. Suddenly, all three stop and turn to face the PCs, growling in unison.
A {@creature Behir|XMM} slinks among the rocks, hunting for a suitable lair among the crags.

name: Tier 2: Ocean
rows: While the PCs are traveling by boat at night, two {@creature Fjord Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Fjord Trolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) begin cutting holes in the underside of the hull, threatening to send everyone into the frigid depths.
A pair of {@creature Sea Lindwurm|NorthlandsWorldbook|Sea Lindwurms} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) rises from opposite sides of the ship, snapping at sailors and tearing at rigging.
A {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM} drifts on a leaky rowboat. Before he can be rescued, he is attacked by a {@creature Hafgufa Spawn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}).

A storm comes suddenly, lightning and thunder accompanied by a lively tune. As the waves and wind rise, a {@creature Fossegrim|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) calls for tribute as it dances upon a nearby shoal.
A sailing ship approaches peacefully. Its owner, an elven {@creature Noble|XMM}, shouts greetings. He claims to seek a mist-shrouded isle where the gods have hidden secret lore.
A monstrous {@creature Hafgufa|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) lurks near the surface of a narrow strait, its teeth appearing as rocks that must be navigated.
A {@creature Young White Dragon|XMM} lands on the deck, shaking off sea spray before pulling barrels around itself and curling up for a nap.
As the PCs sail through the chill waters, a sailor suddenly screams as an {@creature Aboleth|XMM} yanks him over the side.

A wrecked ship founders on the rocks in treacherous waters. Its occupants, a monster hunter and a {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) refuse to be rescued together.

Far from land, a {@creature Raven|XMM} swoops down, cawing and circling the PCs. Simultaneously, the howls of wolves can be heard. Each PC receives Wotan's blessing—granting them {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their next attack roll before the day ends.

name: Tier 2: Road
rows: Two broad-shouldered warriors with golden auras sit at a campfire. These {@creature Einherjar|ToB1-2023} wordlessly offer to share their meal and take offense at any refusal.
A burning wagon blocks travel along the road. Characters who pause here are attacked by three {@creature Trollkin Reaver|ToB1-2023|Trollkin Reavers}.

Three {@creature Buried Lord Vaettir|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) approach along the road, asking for directions to the nearby village that holds a thief who robbed their burial mounds.
A {@creature Ravenfolk Doom Croaker|ToB1-2023} approaches the characters' campsite, threatening them with dire fates unless they pay him.
As the characters watch, a white-feathered {@creature Roc|XMM} swoops down and snatches a horse and cart from the road ahead.

Cold and starving, four {@creature Gnoll Havoc Runner|ToB1-2023|Gnoll Havoc Runners} approach the campfire, pleading for food. Desperation colors their behavior, and violence simmers beneath the surface.

A troupe of three {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook|Skalds} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) sings songs of ancient heroes as they walk down the road, protected by two {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.
Three {@creature Elvish Veteran Archer|ToB1-2023|Elvish Veteran Archers} walk the road, seeking ancient elven ruins. The cruel welcome they've experienced thus far in the North makes them suspicious.

The campsite is suddenly filled with howls, wind, and laughter as two {@creature Wind Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Wind Trolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) leap out of the nearby foliage. They squeakily offer local information in exchange for any visible shiny trinkets or drops of blood.

A grinning red-haired man appears suddenly and introduces himself as Loki. He points at one of the PCs, seemingly at random, and demands a flyting contest. Loki doesn't use his full skill because he doesn't want to hurt the PC's confidence, so he only has a +8 bonus to his rolls.

name: Tier 2: Town
rows: A {@creature Huskarl|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) leads twelve {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} into a village, demanding wergild and tribute for some forgotten insult.

Two rival {@creature Bandit Lord|ToB1-2023|Bandit Lords} confront the PCs in the mead hall, demanding the party face them in a group holmganga. Six {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} hiding nearby wait to ambush the PCs after the duel.

The PCs come upon a burning village. Bodies lie strewn about and ash is heavy in the air. A {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) rushes from behind a building, spots the PCs, and charges, bellowing with fury.
A {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM} celebrates her retirement with a series of nautical-themed competitions that promise grand rewards.

A {@creature Priest|XMM} of Wotan flanked by nine {@creature Priest|XMM|Priests} publicly accuses the local jarl of neglecting the gods. She demands the temple be cleansed of the {@creature Fossegrim|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) plaguing it.

A popular {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) performs in the jarl's hall but uses her music to beguile the audience while she searches for a hidden coffer containing the jarl's prized silver torc.
The local seer collapses in the snow-covered square mid-trance, shrieking the PCs' names as villagers form a wary circle.

A {@creature Wolf Reaver Dwarf|ToB1-2023|Dwarf Wolf Reaver} flees across the rooftops, pursued by two {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} on foot, who are firing bows at him. The reaver hides a relic stolen from the jarl beneath his cloak, but he claims it rightfully belongs to his clan.

Three {@creature Gilitrutt Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Gilitrutt Trolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) rampage through the village, smashing through homes and splintering workshops. Karls flee in panic while the local warriors struggle to organize.

Two {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook|Warpriests} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) of Loki leads four {@creature Swarm of Rats|XMM|Swarms of Rats} through town in a crude capering dirge. Anyone mocking their performance is attacked for irreverent blasphemy.

name: Tier 3: Coast
rows: An iceberg stranded upon the rocky shore ahead suddenly splits apart, freeing an {@creature Ice Devil|XMM}, which fixes its eyes on the PCs.
A trail of ship wreckage and bodies leads to a cave at the edge of a secluded lake, the lair of five {@creature Lake Troll|ToB1-2023|Lake Trolls}.
A wrecked ship contains a rusting statue studded with gems in its hold. It is an {@creature Iron Golem|XMM} that awakens if anyone inspects it.

In the shallow waters just offshore, a fortune in coins and gems lies exposed on the ocean floor. Unfortunately, this is the hoard of a pair of twin {@creature Jorumungkyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}).

Five newly grown {@creature Hafgufa Spawn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) have infested the bay of a fishing village. Their territorial attacks threaten the village's small fleet of ships.

A small longship beaches on the shore, disgorging a howling horde of 25 {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}). A nearby jarl, jealous of the PCs, has ordered this attack, hoping to increase his fame

The PCs come upon a procession of trancing {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} slowly walking into the water until they vanish beneath the surface. Two {@creature Aboleth|XMM|Aboleths} lurk offshore, controlling the victims with their alien minds.

A howling storm threatens to capsize a fishing boat a hundred yards offshore. Six {@creature Wind Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Wind Trolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) dance on rocks, directing the storm with their magic. They claim only a dancing contest will convince them to ease the winds.

An ancient bridge spans a river. The stones of the span are strangely wet despite the conditions of the day. Five {@creature Water Elemental|XMM|Water Elementals} lurk in the river and attempt to pull anyone on the bridge into the river.
A {@creature Sea Hag|XMM} steps out of the water, offering cryptic prophecies in exchange for a personal item from each PC.

name: Tier 3: Forest
rows: Six {@creature Werewolf|XMM|Werewolves} and two {@creature Nightgarm|ToB1-2023|Nightgarms} huddle around the body of a well-dressed {@creature Werekin|NorthlandsWorldbook}. When the PCs are spotted, one grows that "outsiders must be to blame!"

A mournful voice from a nearby barrow bids the PCs to enter, promising hospitality if they do. Upon entering, they meet a {@creature Buried Lord Vaettir|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) who needs them to recover his ancestral blade, recently stolen by a {@creature Skein Witch|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}).

One of {@creature Boreas's Chosen|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) leads four {@creature Frost-Afflicted|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) in a deathly chant as they perform a complicated ritual around a restrained {@creature Treant|XMM}.

Two bickering {@creature Thrudgelmir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thrudgelmir Giants} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) drag a {@creature Worg|XMM} into a stone-ringed clearing. The beast snaps and snarls, unwilling to serve as the sacrifice for their ritual.

A massive bear emerges from the trees and transforms into a strapping, bearded man who introduces himself as the {@creature Bear King|ToB1-2023}. He challenges one of the PCs to a wrestling match, offering magical mead as a prize. He has a +9 bonus to Athletics.
A band of six {@creature Hill Giant|XMM|Hill Giants} thrashes loudly through the woods, trying to drive out escaped captives hiding in the trees.

An ancient spire of metal and crystal marked with elven runes crackles with energy as three {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Lightning Giants} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) direct power into it.

In a forest clearing, four {@creature Fenrikyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) work to slaughter a herd of goats while three {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} cower beneath an overturned cart.

A {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023} claiming to represent Wotan sits on a boulder in a clearing. She says the All-Father challenges the PCs to battle a nearby {@creature Purple Worm|XMM} to prove their worth.
A mountain stream runs red with blood. Hidden upstream, two {@creature Swarm of Ravens|XMM|Swarms of Ravens} feast upon a half-buried corpse marked with runes.

name: Tier 3: Glacier/Tundra
rows: A {@creature Frost Giant|XMM} leads a herd of four {@creature Mammoth|XMM|Mammoths}, their tusks painted in warding runes intended to drive off famine spirits.
A {@creature Remorhaz|XMM} feasts on the blackened corpse of a massive jotun. The giant's body is scorched as if by lightning and bears clear signs of multiple blunt impacts.

A grand carriage pulled by four {@creature Winter Wolf|XMM|Winter Wolves} and controlled by two {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook|Trollkin Berserkers} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) holds the {@creature Snow Queen|ToB1-2023} on her way home.
Two {@creature Liosalfar|ToB1-2023} step out of a snowstorm, declaring that fate has marked the characters for death.
A trail of frozen blood and scattered limbs leads to an icy cave, the lair of three {@creature Blood Hag|ToB1-2023|Blood Hags}.
Roused by foul magic, a warband of ten {@creature Vættir|ToB1-2023} marches across the glacier, re-enacting some ancient battle. They view the PCs as their old enemies.
High on a ridge, four {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} trigger an avalanche from hidden positions behind jagged ice berms. They hurriedly descend to attack PCs trapped by the falling snow.

A {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023} appears, begging the PCs to rescue her lover, a {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}), who has been beguiled by the {@creature Snow Queen|ToB1-2023}. If the fey daughter of Boreas slays her love, he will never win a seat in Valhalla.
A pack of six {@creature Rime Worm|ToB1-2023|Rime Worms} slithers across the snow, scouring the land of anything edible.

Thunderous footsteps accompany the sight of two {@creature Mammoth|XMM|Mammoths} slowly pulling a sled holding a dead {@creature Frost Giant|XMM}. The body is bedecked in funerary garb and holds a ceremonial axe.

name: Tier 3: Hill/Mountain
rows: A small warband of four {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} and two {@creature Winter Wolf|XMM|Winter Wolves} drags sleds heavy with plunder. Upon spotting the PCs, they raise their bloody banner and call out a challenge.
A deadly rain of boulders plummets from the sky. On the ridge above, two {@creature Storm Giant|XMM|Storm Giants} throw huge stones and shatter them with lightning, laughing at their game.
A ragged hermit offers to lead the characters to an abandoned dragon's hoard for a share of the trove. During a treacherous climb, it reveals itself as a {@creature Stuhac|ToB1-2023}.
Three {@creature Fire Giant|XMM|Fire Giants} haul a wagonload of iron and silver ore toward their mountain forge, accompanied by two {@creature Hell Hound|XMM|Hell Hounds}.
Four {@creature Einherjar|ToB1-2023} sit around a burning fire, boasting of killing many giants. If the characters fail to acknowledge their greatness, the warriors attack.
A rime-covered statue blocks a narrow ravine. It is a {@creature Stone Golem|XMM} that attacks anyone attempting to pass.
Among the icy peaks, the PCs discover a deserted encampment. Tracks lead to a nearby cavern where skaldic explorers hang suspended in ice, guarded by their {@creature Stuhac|ToB1-2023} murderer.

The crumbling ruins chime with an otherworldly sound as a towering figure wearing golden armor and a concealing robe appears. A {@creature Herald of Blood|ToB1-2023} demands a sacrifice of the PCs' blood, promising death if they refuse.

The sky darkens and the PCs hear a roar as {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) lands with a crash. He demands they give their most powerful item to him as tribute, or he will destroy them.

A {@creature Cloud Giant|XMM}, a {@creature Frost Giant|XMM}, and a {@creature Stone Giant|XMM}, meet around an ancient obelisk. If they discover the PCs listening nearby, they band together and attack.

name: Tier 3: Ocean
rows: The ship moves through the misty sea toward what appears to be a small rocky island. As the land comes into view, what had seemed stone now is revealed as the hide of a slumbering {@creature Hafgufa|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}).

A {@creature Krake Spawn|ToB1-2023} explodes from the icy water to wrap the ship in slimy tentacles. It roars a name unknown to the PCs and reaches toward a chest hidden in a false compartment, unknown to the PCs.

Two {@creature Sea Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Sea Giants} rise from the waves on a tower above and behind the ship. One speaks a riddle in a booming voice, and then waits expectantly. But it won't wait for long.

Waves threaten to capsize the ship as two {@creature Hafgufa|NorthlandsWorldbook|Hafgufas} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) breach the surface, battling each other viciously. The winner gets to eat the ship and its passengers.
Four {@creature Lindwurm|ToB1-2023|Lindwurms} slash through the waves like spears, spreading out to circle the ship.
As the ship moves through a wreckage strewn strait, an {@creature Adult Sea Dragon|ToB1-2023} rises amid the flotsam, demanding the PCs pay a toll in "shining gold" or meet its challenge in battle.
The sea turns glassy still as the wind dies. Moments later, a whirlpool swirls open nearby, threatening to drag the ship down into the depths.

A forest of heads emerges from the waves as two Cold-Water {@creature Hydra|XMM|Hydras} rise from the icy depths. Roaring with multiple mouths, they strike together, one slamming the hull and crew while the other snaps at the sails and rigging.
Six dangerous reavers ({@creature Pirate|XMM|pirates}) in a swift knarr attack from the sea fog, hurling flaming tarpots to set the sails ablaze.

As the PCs travel along the coast, a group of bedraggled {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) calls out to them from an uninhabitable spit of land. They need rescue before a pair of {@creature Fjord Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Fjord Trolls} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) and their {@creature Sea Lindwurm|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) pet return.

name: Tier 3: Road
rows: A brightly decorated wagon approaches, pulled by plodding {@creature Mule|XMM|mules}. The three sisters sitting on the wagon's bench claim to be seers and offer the bravest of the PCs a prophetic reading.

Traveling late, the PCs come upon a campsite where a skald tells stories of horror and nightmares to a company of petrified {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners}. The skald is actually a {@creature Fear Smith|ToB1-2023}, and his "attendants" are magically disguised {@creature Bugbear Stalker|NorthlandsWorldbook|Bugbear Stalkers}.

Five {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook|Trollkin Berserkers} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) burst from the rock in a howling ambush. Nearby, a {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023} watches over the battle.

A crumbling longhouse seems to offer shelter from the storm. Yet while the elderly couple is welcoming, the two {@creature Runewright|NorthlandsWorldbook|Runewrights} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) who control them are decidedly not.

A {@creature Herald of Blood|ToB1-2023} stands atop a wind-swept outcropping, preaching of the end times to four Ragnarok cult {@creature Witch Apprentice|NorthlandsWorldbook|Witch Apprentices} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) who chant and sway in time to his words.

As snow falls and the fire dims, the ground heaves as two {@creature Corpse Mound|ToB1-2023|Corpse Mounds} crawl from the frost-covered ground, revealing bones and broken weapons from some ancient battle.

Eight {@creature Gnoll Havoc Runner|ToB1-2023|Gnoll Havoc Runners} and five {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs} circle the party's camp at night, silent as drifting snow. When a spellcaster takes a watch, they strike from multiple directions.

A single {@creature Fenrikyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) pads onto the road, its red eyes fixed on the PCs. Four other {@creature Fenrikyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) stalk the party from the sides of the road, ready to strike.

The snowfall that began earlier in the day abruptly howls into a full blizzard, obscuring the road ahead in a blanket of swirling white. From this winter shroud, an {@creature Ice Devil|XMM}, bound by one of the PCs' enemies, ambushes them.

A dozen {@creature Beli|ToB1-2023} flash in and out of sight, tormenting four panicked {@creature Merchant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Merchants} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) and a dying {@creature Guard|XMM}. One merchant begs for help, while another clutches a stolen relic still slick with ice and bound in elfskin.

name: Tier 3: Town
rows: The PCs dream of a crooked snowy mountain peak in the Bleak Expanse. Somehow, they know an {@creature Ancient White Dragon|XMM} awaits them with the offer of great treasure in exchange for a noble deed.
Screams and the snapping of timbers accompany five {@creature Hill Giant|XMM|Hill Giants} as they charge into the settlement, throwing boulders and snatching at surprised karls.

A richly dressed {@creature Monster Hunter|NorthlandsWorldbook} parades down the muddy street with six {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}. They boast of their coming hunt for a mythical beast.
A raging {@creature Thuellai|ToB1-2023} ravages a small village. Howling winds shatter rooftops, and icy rain floods the streets, forcing the townsfolk to scramble for shelter.

A Ragnarok {@creature Archmage|XMM} appears from invisibility, inscribing the air with fiery runes. He proclaims a death mark on the PCs before his four loyal {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} rush to strike.

Amidst a blizzard, four {@creature Ice Maiden|ToB1-2023|Ice Maidens} arrive in town demanding the jarl surrender the settlement to the {@creature Snow Queen|ToB1-2023}'s rule or the settlement will freeze before the dawn.
An angry {@creature Swarm of Ravens|XMM} descends on the characters, only to fly away a round later. Onlookers whisper of Wotan's disfavor and the need for atonement.

A {@creature Crawling Claw|XMM} leaves a trail of frozen blood leading into a forgotten basement where a {@creature Blood Hag|ToB1-2023} and four {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics} work to extract more claws from fresh corpses.
Four {@creature Spectral Guardian|ToB1-2023|Spectral Guardians} hover in the jarl's longhouse, accusing the new jarl of oath-breaking and murder while he begs the PCs to aid him.

Hoisting foaming mugs in the mead hall, two {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook|Trollkin Berserkers} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) loudly take credit for one of the PC's deeds. If confronted, they immediately attack, desperate to hide their lies.

name: Tier 4: Coast
rows: Two {@creature Cloud Giant|XMM|Cloud Giants} step off a floating cloud to walk their pet {@creature Behir|XMM} on the shore. The collared {@creature Behir|XMM} takes an instant liking (or disliking) to one of the PCs.
A buried longhouse groans open, releasing an arctic blast of ice and mist as a demonic horn sounds within. Two {@creature Ice Devil|XMM|Ice Devils}, imprisoned long ago, emerge into the light.

At the edge of the water, revealed by a recent rockslide, is a massive stone door clearly marked with Hyperborean symbols. Within the tomb beyond the door, a {@creature Lich|XMM} guards a fragment of the Dominion Orb.
The branch of a titanic tree appears, sticking partially out of the ground. Twelve mind-controlled {@creature Ratatosk|ToB1-2023|Ratatosks} scurry from the branch to attack the PCs.

The PCs stumble upon a strange holmganga. Four {@creature Trollkin Reaver|ToB1-2023|Trollkin Reavers} watch two {@creature Monster Hunter|NorthlandsWorldbook|Monster Hunters} fighting over a sword buried in a giant's skull. They hate interruptions.

A spectral longship floats above the shore, crewed by twelve {@creature Shroud|ToB1-2023|Shrouds}, three {@creature Ghost|XMM|Ghosts}, and two {@creature Deathwisp|ToB1-2023|Deathwisps}. They hunt for living souls to harvest into new crew members.
A lone child in a bear pelt offers the party berries. She vanishes if touched, and a {@creature Skein Witch|NorthlandsWorldbook} appears in her place, growling her name.
Two {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023|Valkyries} descend to address the PCs. They need the characters to escort an old warrior on one last battle so he can perish heroically and earn Valhalla.
A barnacle-encrusted war-horn lies on the shore. When sounded, it calls a {@creature Kraken|XMM}.
A pattern of stones along the shoreline glow faintly blue, forming runes beneath the PCs' feet. A vision of Wotan appears and offers the PCs one absolute truth and one irrevocable curse.

name: Tier 4: Forest
rows: An {@creature Archmage|XMM} completes an eldritch ritual, causing the PCs' names to be written in a vast spider's web stretching between the trees. Eight {@creature Phase Spider|XMM|Phase Spiders} appear.
A barrow door bursts open as a {@creature Pit Fiend|XMM} hauls out a half-eaten warrior. The fiend glares at the PCs and growls, "This one lied. Will you?"
A forest fire comes swiftly and the blaze closes in. Four {@creature Fire Giant|XMM|Fire Giants} step into the PCs' path. One gestures to the open path behind them and says, "Tribute. Now."

The ground rumbles and trees topple. Terrain near the PCs collapses like a sinkhole, and rising out of the depression is a massive {@creature Annelidast|ToB1-2023}, awakened by the ritual of three nearby Cult of Ragnarok {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook|Warpriests} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}).
An {@creature Ancient Green Dragon|XMM} lies curled in an oak grove. One massive eye opens. It sighs deeply and grumbles, "I dreamed you'd come. I suppose you want the truth?"
A {@creature Fire Giant|XMM}'s body, ripped in half, falls in front of the PCs. Jaws dripping with blood, the multiple heads of two {@creature Zmey|ToB1-2023|Zmeys} turn toward the party.

With a shattering sound, felt even more than heard, the ancient standing stone breaks open revealing two {@creature Pact Vampire|ToB1-2023|Dwarf Pact Vampires} wearing faded garments of their old empire. Their blazing eyes fix on the PCs, and their fanged mouths open, hungry for blood.

A frightened {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) runs through the trees just ahead. Behind the skald, howls and growls sound as six {@creature Nightgarm|ToB1-2023|Nightgarms} burst out of the woods in close pursuit.

Four {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} drag a {@creature Bearfolk|ToB1-2023} corpse into the clearing where a {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) of Angrboda chants a ritual. One giant sneers at the party and says, "They're next."
Four {@creature Ghostwalk Spider|ToB1-2023|Ghostwalk Spiders} descend silently, fangs first, from the canopy above.

name: Tier 4: Glacier/Tundra
rows: A blizzard of unimaginable fury forces the PCs to take shelter in a nearby cave. There, they find a wounded {@creature Jotun|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}). He claims the storm is a vengeful {@creature Elemental Locus|ToB1-2023} and promises friendship if the PCs destroy it.
A raiding party of four {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} and six {@creature Winter Wolf|XMM|Winter Wolves} marches across the glacier chanting war songs of Jotunheim.

An enchanted floating sled of crystal, holding the {@creature Snow Queen|ToB1-2023} and four {@creature Ice Maiden|ToB1-2023|Ice Maidens}, descends from the frigid sky. The queen offers the PCs an alliance for a price.

A distorted shriek echoes across the ice as a portal opens near the PCs, disgorging three {@creature Xhkarsh|ToB1-2023|Xhkarsh}. Their dry unified voice speaks into the PCs' minds. "Fate shall be changed."
Seven {@creature Mammoth|XMM|Mammoths} thunder across the icefield, trumpeting in fear and fury. Their eyes lock on the PCs, and the herd turns straight toward them.
A freezing wind rises. High above, an {@creature Ancient Wind Dragon|ToB1-2023} spirals downward with eyes locked on the PCs.
A scorched stone cavern opening yawns beneath a crumbling ruin reaching out of the ice and snow. Three {@creature Remorhaz|XMM} emerge and charge toward the PCs.
A violent tremor opens the glacial surface, revealing a steep stone stairway. Far below, {@creature Hraesvelgr|NorthlandsWorldbook} awakens from magical slumber with a burning need to destroy.
A bolt of lightning strikes a rune-covered standing stone ahead of the PCs. A ground tremor heralds the arrival of a {@creature Lich|XMM} as it bursts up from the ground.
A one-eyed elk speaks in Old Norse, warning the PCs that "the Overlord stirs." Moments later, a {@creature Balor|XMM} arrives to demand silence—or blood

name: Tier 4: Hill/Mountain
rows: A music-loving {@creature Pit Fiend|XMM} refuses to let the party pass without one (or more) of them performing some sort of entertainment.
Four {@creature Fire Giant|XMM|Fire Giants} work around an outdoor forge above a volcanic rift while six {@creature Ettin|XMM|Ettins} pump the bellows. One giant shouts, "Outlanders!"

A shout thunders through the air. In the distance, a {@creature Jotun|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) strides into view. He accuses the PCs of murdering one of his loyal giants, and now demands a holmganga—all the PCs against him.
A strong wind slams down, nearly lifting the PCs from their feet. A {@creature Roc|XMM} circles as another lands and transforms into {@creature Hraesvelgr|NorthlandsWorldbook}.
A {@creature Priest|XMM} of Thor, frostbitten and delirious, begs for help to complete a sacred pilgrimage up a storm-wracked mountain path.
The ground seems to explode as an {@creature Ancient Cave Dragon|ToB1-2023} bursts from beneath the PCs. As it attacks, it screams for the PCs to return what they've stolen.
A cave offers shelter from a blizzard, but as the party steps deeper, four {@creature Guardian Naga|XMM|Guardian Nagas} awaken around a glowing relic.
A thunderous roar sounds from overhead as an {@creature Ancient White Dragon|XMM} dives from the clouds, unleashing its freezing breath on the PCs.

Echoing horns blare as six {@creature Dire Wolf|XMM|Dire Wolves} and six mounted {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} ride ahead of a {@creature Blood Hag|ToB1-2023} on a ghostly elk. Spotting the PCs, they raise their weapons and charge.

Stepping into view, two elderly humans beg for aid. When the PCs least expect it, they transform. The {@creature Queen of Witches|ToB1-2023} and her {@creature Glabrezu|XMM} minion want a specific item.

name: Tier 4: Ocean
rows: Fisherfolk scream from a nearby boat as an {@creature Ancient Sea Dragon|ToB1-2023} breaches beside them. It smashes the fishing boat and then turns toward the PCs' ship

Three longships close fast, boarding lines already flying. On each, a {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM} leads four {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook|Trollkin Berserkers} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) and twenty {@creature Pirate|XMM|Pirates} under a reaver's banner.
A sailor opens a newly caught fish and finds a rune-etched bottle. Frost rises from the bottle as a {@creature Lich|XMM}'s voice echoes from the glass. "You found my heart. I come for yours."
A tentacle slams into the deck, splitting the mast in half. The sea churns violently as a {@creature Kraken|XMM} rises.
A whirlpool churns into existence as a {@creature Shoggoth|ToB1-2023} rises from its century-long slumber beneath the waves.
As a storm rages around the PCs, two {@creature Slow Storm|ToB1-2023|Slow Storms} take shape.

A longship carved from ice emerges from the mist. Its {@creature Ice Maiden|ToB1-2023} captain and crew of 14 {@creature Frost-Afflicted|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) seek captives to bring to the Bleak Expanse.
An unmarked burial ship drifts past, its sail shredded and its deck strewn with frostbitten corpses clutching swords. No wind moves it, yet it travels against the current.

Standing on a spar of ice, the guttural voice of a {@creature Deep One Priest|ToB1-2023} rises into a screaming chant as two {@creature Dragon Eel|ToB1-2023|Dragon Eels} erupt out of the water. The priest points at the PCs' ship and the eels surge forward.

Two {@creature Roc|XMM|Rocs} circle the ship while four {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics} of Ragnarok leap from the titanic birds, flying down by some sort of magic. In mid-air they hurl spells while the rocs screech in fury.

name: Tier 4: Road
rows: Four {@creature Savager|ToB1-2023|Savagers} growl a warning before returning to feasting on the corpses of two {@creature Mage|XMM|Mage Apprentices}. A third apprentice hides in a tree nearby, frantically waving at the PCs for aid.
An {@creature Alehouse Drake|ToB1-2023} lounges in a nearby tree, the base of which is surrounded by broken ale barrels. The sad but friendly drake needs help finding a new tavern to call home.

An exhausted {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) leads a procession of three charmed {@creature Purple Worm|XMM|Purple Worms}. If she stops playing, they'll attack.
With a howl, something massive crashes onto the road. When the dust settles, an {@creature Ancient White Dragon|XMM} with a broken wing claws free from the debris and roars.

A child in a bear pelt blocks the trail, offering wild berries and a riddle. If ignored, she vanishes, and the {@creature Lord of the Hunt|ToB1-2023} charges from the woods to murder the PCs for their rudeness.

While the PCs are enjoying a roadside lunch with a passing {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}), a {@creature Ravenfolk Doom Croaker|ToB1-2023} leading a band of ten {@creature Einherjar|ToB1-2023} arrives to murder the viking for offending Freyja.
Hoisting the bodies of those they've already slain, a rampaging warband of six {@creature Hill Giant|XMM|Hill Giants} follows a {@creature Son of Fenris|ToB1-2023} toward a nearby town.
The party sees a vision of themselves, battle scarred and wounded, each escorted by a different {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023}.

Four panicked {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} ride past the PCs, screaming a warning. Behind them comes a Jotunheim raiding party of two {@creature Troll|XMM|Trolls} and four {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres} led by a {@creature Storm Giant|XMM}. They beat their weapons on their chests and shields as they march down the road.

Two {@creature Raven|XMM|Ravens} speak in chorus, warning the PCs not to break a circle of iron stakes just off the road. A corrupted {@creature Solar|XMM} is held within, bound in runes of frost and rage.

name: Tier 4: Town
rows: Following omens given to them by the Cult of Ragnarok, {@creature Hraesvelgr|NorthlandsWorldbook} uses a blizzard for cover as he leads his two {@creature Ettin|XMM|Ettin} minions to attack the town.

Two rival {@creature Archmage|XMM|Archmages} from southern lands appear in a flash of light, declaring that portents have named the village the PCs are visiting to be the site of their long-awaited arcane duel.
A misguided {@creature Priest|XMM} of Thor publicly shatters an ancient artifact in the middle of the market, inadvertently summoning a {@creature Balor|XMM}.
Townsfolk hastily pack wagons with their belongings. Two {@creature Dread Skeljaskra|NorthlandsWorldbook} have been spotted emerging from nearby hills.
An {@creature Adult Cave Dragon|ToB1-2023} awakens from a century of slumber beneath the town built atop its resting place.

Enraged at the desecration of their sacred grove, a triad of {@creature Skein Witch|NorthlandsWorldbook|Skein Witches} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}) bursts into the jarl's longhouse, intent on murdering the entire community.
A {@creature Dragon Turtle|XMM} climbs out of the harbor and suns itself in the market. The turtle demands to be fed or it will destroy the entire town.
The great dragon is dead. Now, the beast's incredible hoard is brought before the jarl. Unfortunately, the "treasure" turns out to be two {@creature Hoard Golem|ToB1-2023|Hoard Golems}.
Screams rise from the outskirts of the settlement as four {@creature Oni|XMM} rampage into view while an {@creature Archmage|XMM} incinerates villagers with spell after spell.

After the jarl announces one of his karls stole his prized amulet, six {@creature Shield Guardian|XMM|Shield Guardians} of the ancient dwarven empire march out of the harbor. They begin laying waste to the everything in sight.

name: Transformative Slime Table
rows: The creature is polymorphed into a {@creature sticky slime|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} for 1 hour.
The creature is polymorphed into an {@creature emberbat|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} for 1 hour.
Mushrooms grow from the creature's head until it takes a long rest.

The creature glows bioluminescent green in the dark until it takes a long rest. It emits dim light in a 10-foot radius and has disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks to hide while in darkness, and creatures have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight to spot it.

name: Travelling in the Chetwood
intro: The Loremaster can use the following table if Player-heroes decide to venture into the deep parts of the Chetwood or its more dangerous regions near the {@book Midgewater Marshes|TLotRR|8|The Midgewater Marshes} or the {@book Weather Hills|TLotRR|8|The Weather Hills}. Simply roll a {@dice d12} and consult the table below.
rows: A Stone-Troll is tearing through the Chetwood, making no effort at subtlety or stealth. It spots the Player-heroes and immediately moves to attack, in search of a fresh meal.
A Chetwood hunter fires an arrow at the Player-heroes from a concealed position some distance off. They have mistaken them for a party of Orcs in the shadowy light of the forest.
The Player-heroes come across an abandoned cabin that appears to have been ransacked by Goblins, with signs of a bloody struggle.

The Player-heroes notice they are being tracked by a small pack of wolves. If they don't succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Hunting|TLotRR}) check to throw them off, they'll likely attack in the coming hours.

Caught in a morass of mud concealed by a layer of leaves and lichen, the characters sink and find themselves trapped. They will need to succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check, otherwise the struggle to get free will cause them to suffer one level of {@condition exhaustion} and lose a day of travel.
Goblins have come down from the Weather Hills to scout the Chetwood. They have spotted the Player-heroes and will try to ambush them.

The Player-heroes encounter the Forester of Archet himself. Depending on the nature of their errand, he may aid them or offer them insight into the goings-on of the Chetwood. He can also easily guide them back to Archet.

name: Troll-Holes
intro: The Trollshaws are literally riddled with caves, opened or dug by Trolls to serve as their lairs. The Loremaster can use the table below to quickly and easily come up with a unique location for a Troll-hole.
rows: The Player-heroes begin to explore a cave that seems both shallow and abandoned. But looks are deceiving and when they find their way deeper into the cave, they suddenly come face-to-face with a fearsome {@creature Great Cave-troll|TLotRR}!
A large tree has split wide open at its base and descends into a shallow, muddy hole that serves as lair to a {@creature Stone-troll Chief|TLotRR}. It is slippery and difficult to navigate.
A once magnificent tower that has collapsed in on itself has become the home of a {@creature Stone-troll Robber|TLotRR}. It is of dubious stability and could cave in entirely at any time.

A cave that goes no more than a few feet into the side of a small stone hill is as close to a traditional Troll-hole as one can imagine, and could easily be avoided were it not so close to the {@book East Road|TLotRR|8|The Great East Road}.

A small pool of water with a low waterfall coming off a stone rise serves as the home to a {@creature Stone-troll Robber|TLotRR}, who wades into the water before ducking beneath the falls and coming up on the other side in an easily overlooked lair.
The characters stumble upon a {@creature Cave-troll Slinker|TLotRR} who is tearing away at trees and rocks, freeing an opening leading to a cave.
The Player-heroes stumble upon a Troll that has been turned to stone by the sun while within sight of its Troll-hole. A {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals a lesser Hoard.

name: Unstable Form
rows: The stress of your Transformation becomes too much. You die. You cannot be restored to life by any spell below level 5.
Your form becomes fragile. Your Hit Point Maximum is half your normal maximum.
Your body starts to lose cohesion. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}.
Your body's metabolism quickly drains your energy. You gain 2 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels.
You have trouble processing what is happening. After rolling {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of your first turn.
Your limbs weaken. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (in all modes of movement) decreases by 15 feet and cannot be increased.
Your body does not react quickly to mental commands. You cannot take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}.
You are distracted by your changing form. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.
Your body becomes unable to fight off attacks. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.
You become clumsy. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws and Dexterity ability checks.
You lose blood or other vital fluids during your mutations. You cannot add your Constitution modifier to any {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} spent to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Speaking is difficult. You can only utter one word during each turn. This does not hamper spellcasting.
Your lower limbs become more powerful. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 5 feet.
Your flesh becomes more hardy. You start the day with 4 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} per Transformation Stage.
Your body's systems are enhanced. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}.

name: Unusual Weather
rows: Northern lights descend in writhing streams and stir anger among the crew.

During a blizzard at sea, the sky turns red, and the snowflakes burn like cold fire for {@dice 1d10} minutes. For each minute of the shower, the GM makes a +10 ranged attack against the ship. On a hit, the ship takes {@damage 3d6} Bludgeoning damage and {@damage 1d6} Fire damage. The Fire damage ignores the ship's {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} and lights the ship on fire. It takes 2 minutes and a {@dc 10} Dexterity check from at least three people to put out the flames.

Strange poisonous whisps rise from the sea to lie upon the waves in a green miasma. Make a single {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw for the entire crew. They have a +3 bonus to the roll. If they fail, all NPCs in the crew have two suffer two levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, both of which end when they complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

The crew member at the helm must make three {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check. The ship loses one-third of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and an NPC crew member for each failed check.

A violent storm hammers the ship with lightning and strong wind. The ship, the crew, and all creatures on deck take {@damage 4d6} Lightning damage. Make a single {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw for all creatures on deck. They have a +3 bonus to the roll. A successful save halves the damage, and a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check by the crew member at the helm halves the damage to the ship.
Ice falls from the sky during a strong wind. Anyone on deck takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage. A successful {@dc 13} Dexterity save halves the damage. The crew sees this as a bad omen.

The wind stills, and the ship encounters a weirdly solid fog for {@dice 1d10} days. In addition to the lack of wind, the {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of all other methods that move the ship, such as rowing, is halved. The fog carries mysterious voices.
The wind dies, and the water becomes utterly still and mirror-smooth. The reflections of the crew and ship are disturbingly changed. The crew sees this as a bad omen.
